name: Barban
lead: Two Defranceschi families in 1945, and the parish where the surname still appears in Croatian records today.
body: Acta Croatica records surviving Defranceschi households in the Labin area at Barban into the present century — one of only four Croatian places where the name is still found.

name: Cerovlje
lead: The municipality Gologorica sits in today.
body: Included here because modern Croatian administration files Gologorica under Cerovlje, so civil records after 1945 are found under this name rather than the village's own.

name: Gologorica
lead: The family's documented seat. A De Franceschi house of 1711 still stands on the main square.
body: Municipality of Cerovlje, central Istria. Roman material has been found here, including a gravestone now in the Pazin museum. The parish church of Saints Peter and Paul carries Renaissance altars and a seventeenth-century baptismal font, and a small Romanesque chapel of the Blessed Virgin keeps fifteenth-century frescoes.
Carlo De Franceschi, the historian, was born here in 1809 — of modest landowners, in his own biographer's phrase, not of gentry. In October 1945 the village still held two Defranceschi families.

**Read on 11 November 2026: the Gologorica baptism books of 1778–1872 and the death book of 1784–1880 (DAPA ZM34K-214, the family's own copy of the Pazin State Archives film; `doc`, level 13 for the cells quoted).** Readers cut every frame from the original image, read every entry and every role, and zoomed every cell that began K-, C-, Ko-, Ka-, Kal-, Cal-, Kov-, Cov-, De- or Fran-: baptisms M01068938–M01068952 (1778–1788) and M01069008–M01069153 (pages 1–145 of the book opened in 1784, to 20 November 1872), deaths M01069226–M01069297 (pages 1–135, 9 January 1784 to 23 January 1880). **No Kovačina and no Kalanj in any role**; the Defranceschi are the godparents, parents and dead already counted in October (a verification, not a discovery), and two spellings were new to the Atlas catalogue: **Defrancaschi** (a godfather's cell of 11 June 1802) and **Di Franceschi**. **The parish priests, as the books show them** (first and last entry read, not appointments): Marcus Bancich to 15 September 1781 and dead on 25 January 1782; the canon Mathias Defranceschi, deputising from 17 September 1781, signing as parish priest from 24 February 1782 and baptising to **26 March 1795**, burying to **6 May 1795** — his death entry of 29 March 1797 calls him «ex Paroch: gallogaz», formerly parish priest of this place; Felix Ant. Bobich from 2 July 1795 (baptisms) and 30 July 1795 (burials), dead on 11 December 1805, aged 43; Antonius Ferdinandus Slocovich from 25 September 1806 to August 1822, with administrators and visiting priests until Franciscus Brusich in June 1824; Petrus Milcetich from May 1835 to March 1862; Blasius Zwölber (administrator from 13 April 1862, parish priest later) to his sudden death on 22 May 1879, then administrators. **Read afterwards, the same day:** the baptisms of 1872–1880 (pages 146–164, frames M01069154–M01069163; Zwölber to 8 April 1879, Jacobus Sajovec administrator from 26 June to 13 August 1879, Joannes Dragovina administrator from 24 August 1879) and the book's index (M01069164–M01069180): no Kovačina and no Kalanj in either. The baptism book ends on 12 February 1880 with «Vedi Nuovo Libro Tom. V.»; that Volume V is not on this reel. The death book's name index was read too (frames M01069298–M01069313; no K section, no Kovačina, no Kalanj), and a card «KRAJ» at M01069314 ends the film item. **Not on the reel:** the death book's Volume IV («Segue libro nuovo Vol: IV», from 23 January 1880) and the baptisms' Volume V; the reels hold no marriage register after February 1788. See [the Kalanj page](/kalanj/) for the nil and the near-name Callagaz.

registers.note: The six undigitised books are the oldest — baptisms 1644–1763, marriages 1656–1781, burials 1646–1777.

name: Gračišće
lead: Eight household censuses across 150 years — the richest register series found anywhere in this project.
body: First recorded in 1199. Held by the Patriarch of Aquileia, then the counts of Gorizia, and from 1374 part of the Duchy of Pazin. Bishop Paskazije of Pićan consecrated the Gothic chapel here in 1486, in his own birthplace.
Glagolitic and Latin graffiti survive scratched into the chapel interior — Croatian, written in Croatian letters, inside a town the maps called Gallignana.

***A son of house 5 who died at Pula.*** *Franciscus Liberatus, baptised in January 1840, son of Joan. Bapt. Defranceschi and Francisca Salomon, is — `inf` — the «Franciscus fil. Joannis Baptae e Gallignana», a day-labourer, who was buried at Pula on 20 November 1875 aged 36; his son Joannes Baptista was born there in 1869 ([the Pula page](/places/)).*

registers.note: Thirty-one of thirty-two books digitised. The status animarum give house-by-house listings roughly every twenty years.

name: Ližnjan
lead: Named by the existing family research as the origin of a line that went to the United States and Germany — and never worked in an archive.
body: The received account gives Ližnjan as one of four directions the family dispersed in, onward to the United States and Germany. No register work has been done on it, and the 1945 census records no Defranceschi household here — which does not disprove the line, but does mean it had already gone by then.
Twenty-four registers survive, baptisms from 1683. Only fourteen are digitised, the lowest proportion of any parish in this study.

**From Pola, 1915:** a boy **«Ivan Defrančeski», born at Ližnjan about 1908, son of Antonio and Justina Visdarich, died at Pola of scarlet fever on 10 December 1915** ([his page](/person/ivan-defranceski-1908/); `doc`) — a Ližnjan child of the 1900s, after the film's baptism books end in 1890.

name: Motovun
lead: One family in 1945 — and 121 of 122 registers digitised, the most complete series in the study.
body: A Venetian hill town whose registers open in 1586. If a link has to be traced through the western, Venetian half of Istria, this is the easiest parish in which to do it.

name: Pazin
lead: A De Franceschi household in the county town in 1684 — a hundred and seven years earlier than this archive had it, and fifty-six years before Kobler's man leaves for Fiume.
body: **«Die 24 huius — Ego qui supra baptizavi Mariam filiam legitimam Francisci de Franceschi et uxoris eius Marinę. Patrini fuerunt Hilarius Celin[?] et Jacoba eiusdem…»** Pazin, *Births 1582, 1614–1624, 1645, 1643–1685*, baptism of **24 March 1684**, read off the film at full magnification on 13 September 2026.

Until then the earliest record of the name at Pazin here was **1791** — two elaborate Latin names, Conraddus Vincentius and Liberatus Francus Xaverius, in a single household. This is a century earlier and it is a family: a father, a wife, a legitimate daughter, two godparents standing.

Its weight is not its age. **Kobler has a Giovanni Battista reaching Fiume from the County of Pazin «intorno al 1740»** — the sentence the whole Fiume argument hangs on — and nobody has ever looked for that man at the end he left from. There is now a documented De Franceschi household in the county town fifty-six years before the date Kobler gives. That is not a connection and is not claimed as one; it is the first time the question can be put to a real household rather than to an assumption.

The index gets this entry wrong twice. It transcribes the surname as «De Francesch», dropping the *-i* the page plainly writes, and it puts **Jacoba — a godparent — into the mother's field**. The mother is **Marina**.

Seven indexed records in all, six of them ours, 1684 to 1859. Six volumes of parish book, the oldest opening in **1582**, and, of them, one page of the oldest volume and the baptism books of 1685–1882 have been read here (below).

**Read on 10 November 2026: the Pazin baptism book from 1785 to 1847 (FamilySearch 9R2F-DPD, images 440–670; `doc` for the entries, `inf` where said).** A second household of the name in the county town, a hundred years after the baptism of 1684: «**Deffranceschi Liberatus Maria**», baptised in December 1790 at house 126 (father «Vincentius», mother «Maria Anna nata Cher-/ner», godparents «ex Paroch: Nobilis Pisinensis»), and «**Conraddus Vincentius Defranceschi**», baptised on 22 February 1793 (father «D. Vincentius», mother «Maria»). These are the two «elaborate Latin names» of the index rows above, now read off the page, and they are **sons of one couple of Pazin**, not of 1791 only: the first died in 1792 (`inf`). Around them stand «**Antonia Covaz nata Defranceschi**» (godmother, 31 July 1791), «**Dna Maria Defranceschi**» (godmother six times, December 1794 – March 1800, `inf` the wife of Dnus Vincentius) and «**Dd. Vincentius Defranceschi**» (godfather, 6 February 1798). **After 1800 the name is not in the book as a parent or a godparent for forty years**; the Gologorica family baptised at Gologorica, not at Pazin. The one later entry: «**Petrus Antonius**», born at S. Vincenti and baptised at Pazin on **8 December 1842**, father not named, mother «**Symphorosa Defrancesc…**, *ancilla*» (the last letters are against the ruled line). **Not closed:** the book is not walked (a few cells unsettled, named in the searched row), the volume's first half (1685–1785) was read the same day (next paragraph); the Pazin marriage book 1655–1785 was read the same day (last paragraph below) and the Pazin burial book 1691–1788 was read the same day (last paragraph below); no Kovačina and no Kalanj in any role in 1785–1847.

**Read on 10 November 2026 as well: the first half of the same volume, 1685 to February 1785 (FamilySearch 9R2F-DPD, images 6–439; `doc` for the entries, `inf` where said).** Every register image was looked at and every cell of the names was read; the Defranceschi cells were zoomed at level 13. **The surname is not a parent anywhere in a hundred years of Pazin baptisms (1685–1784), but the Defranceschi of Gologorica stand at the font.** «**D. Joannes Petrus Defranceschi Gologoricensis**» is godfather on 1 August 1746 (beside the wife of the county's counter-scribe) and «**Dnus Joannes Petrus Defranceschi Gollogoritiensis**» on 5 October 1749; «**Dno Josepho de Franceski ex Gollogoritia**» stands on 19 January 1754 and «**Dnus Joseph Defranceschi Gologoricensis**» on 27 October 1769 beside the widow of an Antonius Covaz; and a priest, «**R. Dnus Mathias Defranceschi ex Golagorizza**», baptises by licence on 14 or 24 April 1769 and is godfather on 15 November 1770 at the baptism of a son of Antonius Covaz. **inf:** these are the Gologorica men already known from the Gračišće books and the Gologorica death register (Giovanni Pietro d. 1781, Josephus d. 1787, the priest Mathias d. 1797); their link to the Covaz of Pazin (the Antonius Covaz who was procurator of the Montecuccoli estate and the «Antonia Covaz nata Defranceschi» of 1791) is the point to follow. **One entry outside Gologorica:** on 31 July 1708 «**Casparus de Franceschi** et **Victoria eius filia ex Sanvicenti**» (Svetvinčenat) stand godparents; no relation is claimed. The baptism of 24 March 1684 (Maria, daughter of Franciscus de Franceschi and Marina) is in the volume before this one. **No Kovačina and no Kalanj in any role in 1685–1785; no priest Josephus is a Defranceschi.** Near-names read and not counted: Tranquilli (*Nobiles Pisinenses*, zoomed: a T), Franul (the Provost and canons), Franetich, Francin, Deffar, Covaz, Callaz/Calaz, Calligarich, Mattich/Mattesich/Matteicich. The book is **not** closed as walked: slips and unsettled cells are named in the searched row.

**Read on 10 November 2026 as well: the Pazin marriage book 1655 to 1785 (FamilySearch 9R26-16F, frames 50–270; `doc` for the entries, `inf` where said).** Every frame was looked at and every cell of the names was read; the Defranceschi, Sanvicenti and Covaz cells were zoomed. **One Defranceschi marriage in a hundred and thirty years: on 18 June 1668 the chaplain Matthias Chianalion married «Andream filium q.m Jacobi Defranceschi de … / De Sanvicenti» (S. Vincenti, Svetvinčenat) and Joanna, daughter of the late Joannes Baptista Hort** (frame 70, left page; level 13: the surname is one clear word, the word struck through before *De Sanvicenti* cannot be read; witnesses read «D. Fabricio Rapiti(?)» and «Dom: Gaspare Ramelio(?)»). His father was dead already. **inf:** this is the town of the *Casparus de Franceschi et Victoria eius filia ex Sanvicenti* who stood godparents at Pazin on 31 July 1708 and of the Symphorosa of 1842; no relation to the Gologorica Defranceschi or to the Pazin household of 1790 is claimed, and the 1684 baptism's Franciscus de Franceschi and Marina do not marry in the frames read. **The Covaz are in the book as a family of Pazin, never beside a Defranceschi:** Antonius Covaz *ex Parochia* [first letter unsettled]-*stoina* marries Catharina, daughter of Franciscus Godina, on **4 June 1735** (frame 182 right, level 13; priest Natalis Collinas, witnesses Gregorius Slocovich and Simon Dequal); he and a Carolus, a Martinus and a Joannes Covaz stand witness at Pazin marriages between 1748 and 1781; **Martinus, son of the late Antonius Covaz, marries on 24 Oct 1762, Ursula, daughter of the late Antonius, on 10 Feb 1772 (house 280), and Joanna, daughter of the late Antonius, on 1 Sep 1780.** **No marriage joins a Defranceschi and a Covaz.** The «late Antonius Covaz» of the entries of 1762, 1772 and 1780 may be one man or more than one, and the book does not say whether he is the Antonius of 1735. **A lead, not a finding:** a family *Cerovaz* (also written Carovaz, Cerouaz) appears in more than thirty entries from 1717 to 1783, once beside Antonius Covaz (30 Nov 1748, frame 216 right); whether the Covaz are a short form of it is not shown. **Gologorica:** a widower «ex Gollagoritia» marries on 20 May 1758 and a widower «Parochiae Gollogoricensi» on 16 Aug 1760 (neither a Defranceschi), a groom «de Parochia Gologoritiae» on 26 Nov 1776, and the parish priest of Gologorica signs on 27 Nov 1776; one groom «de Castro Sancti Vicenti» on 6 Jul 1699 (not a Defranceschi). **No Kovačina, no Kalanj, and no priest Josephus who is a Defranceschi** (Josephus Orlich, Facchinetti, Slocovich, Costanza); the marriage of Vincentius Defranceschi and Maria Anna Cher-ner (c. 1789) is later than 1785. Near-names read and not counted: Franul, Franetich, Francin, Franconich, Tranquilli (a T), Deffar, Caligarich, Kalaz/Callaz/Calaz, Kovačić-type Covacich, Coverliza, Couanich, Luxetich. The book is **not** closed as walked: the unsettled cells and the frames not read are named in the searched row.

**Read on 13 November 2026 as well: the rest of the same marriage volume, frames 271–396 (FamilySearch 9R26-16F; `doc` for each cell quoted, `inf` where said).** The end of the first book (1785–1852: the printed Latin table to 13 July 1812, then Italian and Latin consent acts, loose circulars of 1815 and a house list of 1780) and the whole of the second, *Liber Copulatorum* 1812–1847, which stops in April 1847 on the last leaf shown. Every frame was looked at; the Defranceschi, Covaz, Mattiasich and Kovačina/Kalanj cells were zoomed to level 13, the rest read at page size. **A Defranceschi is named four times, never as a groom and never as a bride:** on **24 June 1812** the witnesses to the marriage of a Giacich of Lovran and a daughter of the Pazin noble Segher are «Dnus Franciscus Covaz Pisinensis. Et Dnus Jacobus Defranceschi ex Gollogoriza» (frame 296, left, level 13); on **22 February 1819** the same Jacobus is witness, with the physician of S. Vincenti, to the marriage of Dnus Josephus, son of the late Antonius Covaz, aged 39, and the noble Theresia Segher, aged 20 (frame 355, right, level 13); on **14 October 1822** a Covaz bride, Theresia, a widow of 35, marrying a pharmacist from Capodistria, has as parents «def: Dnus Antonius Covaz civis» and **«def.a Dna Maria De-franceschi»** (frame 359, right, level 13: the first syllable is hyphenated at the line end, the rest is one clear word); and on **13 September 1842** the witness beside an imperial-royal auscultant is «Carolus De-/framesch[i]», where the letters are D-e-f-r-a-m-e-s-c-h-i, an *m* where *nc* is expected (frame 383, level 13; the spelling is as written and **not settled**, and the man is not placed). **inf:** the Covaz of these entries are one family, in order: Josephus (m. 1819), his widow Theresia Segher (who marries again on 3 July 1826, frame 363) and their son Antonius (m. 1842, frame 383); the bride of 1822 is a daughter of the Antonius Covaz of Pazin whose wife was a Defranceschi. **What this adds to the earlier reading above:** «no marriage joins a Defranceschi and a Covaz» still holds for the frames read, and the record that does join them is a mother's name in a later marriage. It names a *Maria Defranceschi* as a Covaz wife, and it is the thread the Gologorica page noted and did not chase ([a «Maria uxor Antonij Covaz Pisinensis»](/gologorica-line/#liberii1769) at a Gologorica font); whether the two are one woman is **not shown**. **The Covaz and the French mayor (`inf`).** The Gologorica death book records that its register was handed to the Municipality of Pisino on 20 July 1812 «per ordine del Maire S.ʳ Fran.ᶜᵒ […]ovaz» (the capital is not legible there). A history of the Pazin registers (Vlahov, Jelinčić and Doblanović, introduction to *Vjesnik Istarskog arhiva* 11–13, 2008, footnote 33, quoting Božo Milanović, *Hrvatski narodni preporod u Istri*, p. 41–42) names the Pazin mayor of these years as «Kovač (Covaz)». The marriage book has a «Dnus Franciscus Covaz Pisinensis» as witness on 24 June 1812, four weeks before the books were taken (frame 296, left, level 13, checked on the image), and a «Dnus Franciscus Xaverius Covaz Prator» as witness on 20 July 1813 (frame 350, left; the walker's page-size reading, not rechecked). Whether the mayor of the note is this Franciscus is **not shown**; the two fit, and the family is the one of the entries above. **Five Mattiasich/Matiasich entries** (1819, 1827 twice, 1831, 1841) stand in the book (a barber, a shoemaker, a tailor's son, villagers); none of them is joined to a Defranceschi. **Not found in the frames read, at page size or zoomed:** a marriage of Vincentius Defranceschi and Maria Anna Cher-ner (c. 1789) or a Vincentius as witness, groom or father; a Mattiasich × Defranceschi marriage; any Kovačina or Kalanj in any role; a priest Josephus who is a Defranceschi. Near-names read and not counted: Delorenzi, Cherbavaz/Chervavaz (20 Jan 1830, read Cher-vavaz, not Cher-ner), Skalamera/Kalamera (5 Aug 1841; the ending rules out Kalanj), Callaz/Calaz, Franul, Coverlizza and its forms. **The book is not closed as walked:** the cells outside the zoomed ones were read at page size; a struck word in 1835 (frame 324), two clipped right edges, a blot over two 1838 rows (frame 375), the date columns of two frames and the foot of frame 393 are unsettled, and the months June–November 1844 and June–September 1845 have no entries; the last frame of 1847 is April, so later marriages of that year are not in this volume.

**Read on 10 November 2026 as well: the Pazin burial book, May 1691 to April 1788 (FamilySearch 9R2F-FMQ, frames 7–368; `doc` for the entries, `inf` where said).** Every frame was looked at and every entry was read by a reader; every Covaz entry and the cells beginning De-, Fran- or Kov- were looked at again by this session, the Covaz entries of 1736, 1749, 1752, 1761 and 1772 at level 13. **No Defranceschi in any form, in any role, in 97 years of burials — and no Kovačina and no Kalanj.** The deceased, the parent or husband named, the burying priest and the margin were looked at in every entry. That includes the dead of the Gologorica Defranceschi's own century: nobody of that name was buried at Pazin (as the baptisms said, they were buried at Gologorica), and no Franciscus de Franceschi or Marina (the parents of the baptism of 24 March 1684), no Casparus de Franceschi (1708) and no Jacobus or Andreas Defranceschi of S. Vincenti is in the book between 1691 and 1788. A man «Jacobus Defranceschi» who was already dead in 1668 would be in the earlier burial book (9R26-16Y, 1655–1691), which is not read. **The Covaz are in the book as a family of Pazin and a household with house number 70, never beside a Defranceschi.** Fifteen burial entries: **5 July 1736** Joanna, daughter of Antonius and Catharina «Kouaz» (written with a K; five days or fifty-four, the first figure is a long s; the couple of the marriage of 1735); **16 August 1749** Joannes Antonius, son of Antonius Covaz, one year three months, buried in the church of S. Nicolai; **August 1752** Matthias, son of Antonius, whose surname has blotted middle letters (Co?az) and who was buried «in Ecclesia S. Justi Tergesti. Studiosus» (at S. Giusto in Trieste, a student), **15 September 1752** Josephus, son of Antonius Covaz, seven years six months, and **8 January 1753** Catharina, daughter of Antonius Covaz, about five (three children in five months); **4 November 1761 Antonius Covaz himself, «circiter 50», confessed and anointed, buried in the church of S. Nicolai** (no wife or parent named); **29 September 1772** Hieronymus, fifteen, «filius defuncti Antonij Covaz» (house 70), and **27 October 1772** Barbara, three, daughter of Antonius Covaz (house 70); **29 and 2 September 1778** a second Antonius Covaz, «de Carniolia, hic Pisini pro tempore commorantis» (house 167), buries his wife Josepha, about 37, and his son Joannes, «natus Flumine» — born at Fiume — and the same day a servant of Antonius Covaz of house 70 (Antonius Spraha, 26); **19 March 1780** Antonius, son of Antonius Covaz, and **16 October 1780** Barbara, seven years ten months, daughter of «Dni Ant: Covaz» (both house 70; the years cell of the first reads 5 or a looped 0); **16 September 1783** Rosalia, daughter of «Dni Antonij Covaz», one year five months (house 40), and **27 August 1784** Mahdalena, wife of Martinus Covaz, 42 (house 35). **inf:** the «late Antonius» of the marriages of 1762, 1772 and 1780 is the Antonius buried on 4 November 1761; the Mahdalena of 1784 is the Maria Magdalena Strocica who married his son Martinus in 1762; a younger Antonius, called *Dominus*, has house 70 in 1772–1780. Whether the Antonius of 1735 is the Antonius of 1761 is not written in either entry. **Nothing joins the Covaz to a Defranceschi**; no burial entry names an Antonia née Defranceschi. **Where the book says Sanvicenti:** a pauper Matheus ex S. Vicenti (18 Feb 1736), Matthias Mazzan of the parish of S. Vincenti (2 Jun 1750), a pauper Joannes ex S. Vincenti (29 Apr 1755), and Simon Vucussich, the parish priest of Sanvicenti, dead at Pazin on 18 December 1780 (house 130) — none a Defranceschi. **Gologorica:** only a Thomas Kabar «ex Gologoriza» on 12 October 1786. **Priests named Josephus** (Facchinetti, Slocovich, Orlich, Pucich) are not Defranceschi. Near-names read and not counted: Cerovaz (about fifty entries 1704–1787, once beside nothing of the Covaz), Kalaz/Callaz/Calaz (many; no n, so not Kalanj), Calligarich, Franul (the Provost), Franetich, Deffar/Defar, Tranquilli (a T), Covacich, Couaich/Couanich (1699–1701), Coverliza, Cosparaz, Kakaz (1702), Chogouast (1706), «Antonius Frane», a soldier (18 Nov 1775), Godina. The book is **not** closed as walked: the unsettled cells and the gaps are named in the searched row.

**Read on 10 November 2026 as well: the Pazin burial book from 1788 to 1847 (FamilySearch 9R2F-FMQ, frames 369–508; `doc` for the entries, `inf` where said).** The same roll as the paragraph above, from where it stopped. Every frame was displayed whole, as left and right half-page crops, and read once by readers who zoomed every cell they doubted; the two Defranceschi entries, the Covaz entries of 1789, 1793, 1805, 1814 and 1826 and the Kov- cells were looked at again by this session at level 13. It is one table of the old Latin form to 13 July 1812 (frame 438; an index of 1777 on frame 440), a plainer list of the deaths of October 1777 to December 1780 at the back of that item (frames 441–442, which repeats the Covaz of 1778 and 1780 already read on frames 329–334), and then the next book, «Matična knjiga umrlih 1812–1847» (cover on frame 446, first leaf on 447), to 21 May 1847 on frame 506. Where a page writes its year's total, the reader's count of the entries equalled it (1793, 1794, 1795, 1819–1823, 1833–1836, 1841, 1845 and 1846). **Two Defranceschi, both children, and both already in the FamilySearch index as leads.** **14 February 1792** (frame 390 right, leaf 70, house 77, level 13): «**Defranceschi / Liberatus / Fran: Xav: / filius Dni vincentij**», one year, buried by Lucas Mattich, parish priest of Coridico, for the administrator of the vacant provostry — the child baptised at Pazin in December 1790 as «Deffranceschi Liberatus Maria» (house 126; `inf`, close to settled: the Xaverius, the father Vincentius and the age agree; the house number does not and is not explained). **5 March 1793** (frame 393 right, leaf 73, no house number, level 13): a boy of four (a half-sign follows the figure), written «**De Franceschi**» under a first name that was over-written and struck through. **The index reads that name «Anastasius»; at level 13 it begins with a looped C and reads «Constantinus»** (the middle letters are heavy; `inf`). No parent is named, the Praepositus Franciscus Nicolaus da Persich buried him. **inf, a candidate and no more:** the «Constantinus Antonius Josephus» baptised at Kastav on 12 March 1789, son of Vincentius Blasius Defranceschi, would have been three years eleven months old. He is not Conraddus Vincentius (baptised here on 22 February 1793, eleven days earlier), whose burial is not in the book. **No other Defranceschi in any form, in any role, in 59 years of burials** — no Dominus Vincentius, no Maria Anna, no wife or widow, no Symphorosa (1842), no Mathias, canon of Pedena. **No Kovačina and no Kalanj** in any role. Two cells are named because they are not settled: **20 April 1812** (frame 438 left, house 164) «Franciscus **Kov:** (or Rov:) filius Dni Antonij Cam-», a boy of two buried by Simon Dequal — the capital is a K or an R, the surname is cut short at a colon and the father's name runs into the rule; this session's level 13 does not settle it (not counted, not excluded); and **17 July 1791** (frame 389 left, house 81), a struck word under «Sironich Francisca» that ends «-ovina», its swashed capital not a K, its middle not read (not Kovačina, which ends -ačina). **The Covaz of Pazin go on, and never beside a Defranceschi.** **17 September 1789** Martinus, «filius defti Dni Antonij», 47 (house 35, the house of his wife Mahdalena of 1784); **1 January 1793** Catharina, «vidua Antonij», 78 (house 40); **23 March 1793** «Antonius Covaz a Lublana», 60 (a Carniolan, `inf` the Antonius «de Carniolia» of 1778); **26 January 1798** Micael Covaz, a soldier of the Esterházy regiment, 30; **11 June 1805** «Antonius Augusti[nus] Covaz», 67 (house 40); **8 April 1814** «**Maria Vidua defuncti Dni Antonij Covaz**», 69 (house 36; level 13); **2 December 1820** the retired priest Carolus Covaz, 77, «Ex-Parrocus Antonionensis»; **14 August 1823** Dnus Franciscus Xaverius, 53, and **29 December 1823** Maria, «filia def. Dni Antonij Covaz», 57 (both house 33); **13 September 1826** Dnus Joannes Nepom. Covaz, local inspector of schools, 71 (house 63); and on frames 441–442 a child Antonius of 1 year 9 months, 25 January 1778. **inf:** the Catharina of 1793 is the Catharina of the baptism of 1736 and the widow of the Antonius of 1761; the Antonius of 1805 is the Dominus Antonius of house 40 in 1783. **Which Antonius was the husband of the Maria of 1814 is not written, and whether she is the Gologorica godmother is not established.** **Gologorica:** a smith, Blasius Gustincich, and his wife Maria «oriunda ex Gologorica» (20 August and 12 October 1788), a «N. Georgius oriundus ex Gollogorica» (10 January 1789), «Josephus filius Joannis Cris-/Grismanich natus Gollogoricae», 24 (23 March 1805), «Joanna dicta Schinovitza ex Parrochia Gollogoritia», a poor woman who died in the hospital (31 December 1814), and Joannes Udovich Jacobich, an innkeeper, «ex Gol(l)ozgouize», 38 (10 July 1838) — none a Defranceschi. **Gallignana (Gračišće):** Andreas Zulle ex Territorio Gallignanae (16 November 1799), Anna wife of Bartholomaeus Lanza (4 November 1803), Anna wife of Petrus Schlessich, tailor (5 June 1835). **Priests called Josephus**, none a Defranceschi: Josephus Mikotich (substitute chaplain, August 1788), Josephus Slocovich (Provost of Pazin, burying from 23 October 1804 and buried 18 August 1817), Josephus Fachinetti (a priest buried 29 October 1808, 72), Josephus Corinaldi (cooperator 1817), Josephus Seloshek/Jeloushek (cooperator, 1832–1837) and Josephus Brezevich (cooperator, 1844). The canon of Pedena buried on 24 December 1775 was Bartholomaeus Zhersetich, not Mathias Defranceschi. **Near-names read and not counted:** Callaz/Callay/Calaz (about 60 entries, a z not an n, houses 92 and 163–193), Calligarich/Calligari, Coverlizza/Covertizza (and the cooperator priest of that name), Cerovaz (about 50 more entries), Corich, Covich, Cocich, Casalaz, Castellaz, Migliavaz, Ladavaz, Gombaz, Deffar/Defar, Dequal (the Provosts and a Mathias Dequal), Franul, Franichi, Francich, Frantel, Defvilla, De Rapicio, Decorte, de Foscarini, Dofvilla, De Tranquilli (a T), «Antonius Frane» (a soldier). **Not claimed:** this is **not** a walked book, and the end-of-item cards on frames 509 and 511 were not opened (507, 508 and 510 were). Gaps and unsettled cells are in the searched row, among them: the women's deaths of 1775 (frames 302–307 right are blank leaves and bleed-through; 309 right and 310 right carry women of January–March 1776; the year's total of 52 is not on the frames); and in 1843 a pencil page number, 49, is skipped between 28 January and 26 February.

**Read on 10 November 2026 as well: the earlier Pazin burial book, March 1655 to May 1692 (FamilySearch 9R26-16Y, frames 0–92; `doc` for the entries, `inf` where said).** The book runs on without a break into the one read the same day (May 1691 onward), so the Pazin burials are now read from **24 March 1655 to April 1788** (the gaps are named below). Every frame was looked at and every entry read by readers; the cells that bear on the three families and on the Hort bride of 1668 were zoomed. **No Defranceschi in any form, in any role, in 37 years — no Kovačina, no Kalanj, no Covaz, no priest Josephus, no Gologorica, Sanvicenti or Gračišće person.** **Jacobus Defranceschi «de Sanvicenti», dead before the marriage of 18 June 1668, is not in the Pazin burials of 1655–1668**, and neither are the Franciscus de Franceschi and Marina of the baptism of 24 March 1684 in the burials of 1684–1692. **Not excluded:** the lower two thirds of the water-damaged page of 23–25 December 1658 (frame 7 left), five faint struck entries of 1655 (frame 4), two illegible entries of April–May 1664 (frame 19 right) and ten weeks between 5 June and 19 August 1668 (facing pages, frame 32) are not read, and a man who died before June 1668 could stand in any of them; no entry at all stands for December 1672 to February 1673. If he was buried at Sanvicenti the entry is in a book that is not on this film (worklist 306). **The Hort of the 1668 marriage:** one entry reads *Hort* plainly, **31 August 1665** (frame 21 right, page 19, level 13), «Joannes filius f?onnii Hort, two months old» (the father's word begins with a long-tailed f, so it is not Joannis; it may be Franci(sci)); no mother, no burial place. The same family seems to stand in the book in two other spellings: **10 March 1689** «puella filia Jacobi [looped Z, Ch or H]ort(h), dicta Joanna» (frame 79 right), then **Jacobus «Kortich/Kertich» alias Drubista** with his son Rochus, 18 August and 19 October 1689 (frames 81–82). **Cells the readers read as Port, Rort or Rost**: Joanna daughter of the late Catharina Port, about 24 (17 Oct 1666), Franciscus Port, about 31 (5 Jun 1668, thirteen days before the marriage), Antonius son of the late Franciscus Port (8 Aug 1669), a Franciscus Rost, about 60, and Joanna his widow, about 55 (3 and 29 Mar 1680), and four more of 1676–1680; the scribe's capital is closer to his P and R than to his H. **Nothing here says whether any of them is kin to Joanna, daughter of the late Joannes Baptista Hort; the entries are recorded, not joined. The Pazin baptism book of 1643–55 writes that family Port, and tells Joanna's own baptism (read the paragraph on the baptisms of 1643–55 below).** **One Covaz-shaped cell:** «Margarita filia Antonij Ce?ouaz», about ten, 29 October 1672 (frame 42 right, level 13): there is an e after the C and no separate Covaz shape, so it leans to Cerovaz; it is not counted. Cerovaz otherwise appears a handful of times in the book (1664–1688), never beside a Covaz. **Near-names read and not counted:** Kalaz/Calaz/Chalaz/Kolaz (many, Pazin 1655–1690: a judge Martinus Kalaz about 50 in 1660, a judge Andreas Kalaz about 75 in 1687; no n), Caligarich, Calcich, Calin- (an edge cut, 1679), Calinaj (1677), Culinas (1679), Kaglia (a midwife, 1667), Layn and Lain (1661–62), Couacich/Covacich (1664, 1690), Francinich/Fracinich/Franinich (a priest Philippus Francinich, 1670–76), Franich (a priest Andreas Franich, 1669), Dequal, Stancovich, Chalcich. One cell is odd and is not Kalanj as read: «Matthias filius Antonij ?alonij», 18, 20–25 August 1661 (frame 12 right; the first letter is a or H, the fourth an o). **The priests** who bury are Joannes Belich, Matthaeus Stancovich, Thomas Coslian, Jacobus Rampelich (the Provost), Matthaeus Chiavalon/Chacahori, Michael Zadanich, Andreas Vranich, Joannes Calcich, Antonius Cergna and Matthaeus Sianolon; none is a Josephus (a lay Josephus Rogovich/Bogovich died in 1685 and 1691; a «Dns Josephus» of about 55 whose surname is overwritten, buried 3 March 1672, is not called a priest). **Unsettled:** every reader's report names its own; the book is **not** closed as walked.

**Read on 10 November 2026 as well: the Gologorica registers themselves, searched for the Covaz wife of the godparents of 1781 and 1785 (DAPA ZM34K-214, the family's own copy of the film, 118 frames; `doc` for the entries, `inf` where said).** The frames: **M01068915–M01068952** (the baptism book II, 3 January 1764 to December 1788); **M01068953–M01069007** (the bound book of 1770–1789: a house list of 130 houses, the baptisms of boys from 1 July 1770 to 17 September 1781, of girls to 26 July 1781, the burials of men from 1770 to January 1789, of women from September 1770 to November 1787, and 120 marriages from 1 July 1770 to 27 January 1789); **M01069199–M01069223** (an Italian perpetual calendar of adult deaths, compiled in 1806 from 1646 and kept up to 1829, each name under its day of the month with the year of death). Every page was read by readers, who zoomed their doubtful cells; the entries relied on below were looked at again by this session. **Maria Covaz is in these books four times, always as a godmother, never as a bride, a mother or a corpse.** **20 June 1781:** Antonius Aloysius, born 12 June to Joannes Andreas Nicolò de Castro Rozzi and Marianna daughter of Dominus Josephus Defranceschi, baptised by the canon Mathias Defranceschi by licence of the parish priest; godparents Dominus Joannes Baptista Defranceschi and «Maria uxor Dni Antonij Covaz Pisinensis» (baptism book II, M01068940 right, last entry of the page); **the same baptism is entered a second time in the book of boys' baptisms (M01068965 right), where she is «Domina Maria Covaz Pisinensis»** (no *uxor*, no husband, no parents, no origin beyond Pazin). **6 January 1785:** the entry already told on the Gologorica page, in two registers: «Antonius, ejusque uxor Maria Covaz ex Pisino» (book II, M01068944 right, no. 36, with the officiant Carolus Covaz, canon of Antignana). This is a re-read of a known entry, not a find. **4 October 1787 (M01068946 right, entry 61 of the book's own numbering, the first of the page; looked at by this session):** the godparents are «viduus Antonius **?ovis** ex Petina» and Hellena wife of Josephus de Franceschi. The archive had read the surname as *Bovis*, a second reader as *Covis*; the initial is a large looped capital unlike the scribe's plain C in *Catharina* and *Cui*, and **it is not settled whether it is a B or a C**. If this Antonius is the godfather of 1785 he is a widower of Pedena by 1787, which would put Maria Covaz's death between January 1785 and October 1787 (`inf`, and only if the cell reads Covis); **no burial of any Maria Covaz is in the women's register for those years.** **Everything else that is Covaz-shaped is not Covaz:** «Ancich alias Cobaz» (a Gologorica house, 1772–1787: house 127 in the house list, 106 in the calendar), Covacich of Novaki and Cerovlje (1771–1785), Crismanich alias Covacich (a death of 1817 in the calendar), a «Michiele Co?va di Cargnia» (22 December 1762, a man of Carnia). **What the books do not hold (nil):** no Covaz bride or groom in 120 marriages 1770–1789; no Covaz burial in the men's or women's registers 1770–1789; no Covaz in the death calendar for any day of the year, 1646–1829; no Covaz, Carolus or Antonius, as a parent in the baptisms of 1764–1788; no Maria née Defranceschi as bride or corpse; no Kovačina or Kalanj in any form; no priest Josephus except Josephus Deprato, parish priest of Cerovlje (witness of 1781, burier of 1788–89, d. 17 October 1801), who is a Deprato. **So Maria Covaz is a Pazin wife who stands at the font of Gologorica; nothing in these books says whose daughter she was or whether she was born a Defranceschi.** The only book that could say is Pazin's own (worklist 310). **Carolus Covaz, canon of Antignana** buries the old Joannes Petrus Defranceschi on 9 September 1781 (M01068980 right, no. 36; the words between *per* and his name are faint) and baptises in 1785; the death calendar has no Carolus Covaz. **New to the archive from these pages:** **5 February 1781** (M01069002 right, the first entry under the year 1781; looked at by this session) «Dnus Petrus Baxa filius Supani Josephi [of Andovci] copulatus est cum honesta Virgine **Rosalia filia Dni Josephi Defranceschi**» before Marcus Banich, with Josephus Deprato, parish priest of Cerovlje, and the syndic Joannes Judreicich as witnesses: she is the Rosalia of the godparent entries 1769–1776, and **inf** the «Rosalia Baxa uxor Petri ex Lindar» who stands godmother at house 36 on 20 July 1789; **9 November 1782** (M01069002 right, no. 61) the witnesses of the marriage of Josephus Flegar and Mariana Deprato are «Antonio Defranceschj, et Margavcka de Franceschj, ex hac Parochia»; **9 February 1784** (M01069003 right, no. 70; looked at by this session) a witness is «Domino Jacobo de Franceschi» of Gologorica, alongside the syndic Martinus Zabran; Margaretta Ancilla, 22, daughter of Josephus and Hellena, is buried on 25 April 1783. **Dates the calendar fixes (all `doc`):** Leonardo, 76, 14 March 1773 (buried in the Arca of Dominus Petrus); Gioanni Pietro, 86, house 36, 8 September 1781; Giuseppe, 64, house 36, 30 December 1787 (buried 31 December; the death register writes the surname *Francasolj*); Antonio q. Leonardo, 60, house 29, 17 September 1802; Gio:Batta q. Giuseppe, 60, house 17, 23 January 1813 (a later hand). **The priest Mathias: the year is settled (1797), the age is not.** He baptises by licence from 1772 as «Mathias Defranceschi», canon of Pedena, gives Banich the last rites (the calendar has Banich d. 25 January 1782, aged 73), signs the burials as parish priest from 12 May 1782 and the marriages from July 1782 («Franceschj»), and from November 1785 «Joannes Mathias de Franceschj». **The back endleaf of the calendar lists the parish priests: line 12 is «Joan: Matthias Defranceschi», with «ab anno 1785» added above and «obiit … Martii 1797» to the right; the calendar itself has «Rev.do Sig.r Gio:Mattia Defranesch[i] Paroco del Luogo, d'anni 66», 29 March 1797 (M01069207 right). The death register has him on 29 March, aged 62 (M01069235), with no year on the entry: the heading over the run is «179» with the last figure under a blot (this archive had read it 1798), but the run goes on in date order to 6 November and the facing page opens with 22 November 1797, so the entry is 1797 (`inf`, looked at again on 10 November 2026).** Day and year now agree in the calendar, the priest list and the register; the age, 62 against 66, does not, so he was born about 1736 or about 1731. The calendar's own title page says it was gathered in 1800 (see the corrections page); the compiling year is a separate small question. Worklist 309 is done except for his first and last signatures as parish priest. **The two Joannes Baptista, once more:** he is «filius Leonardi» on 24 September 1769, «filius Dni Josephi» on 28 December 1769, 14 September 1770, 20 February 1772 and 15 September 1773 (a witness), and «q.n Leonardi filius», a weaver, who marries Theresia Grah of Cherbune on 9 June 1774, and «q. Leonardi» again in 1779–80; the baptism book II of 1783–1788 keeps three couples apart by their wives (Joannes Baptista and Theresia née Grah; Joannes Baptista, son of Josephus, and Catharina née Sablich of Buccari; Joannes Baptista «defti Leonardi» and Catharina Deprato, 11 November 1786). The books settle nothing about the identification of the man who was «filius Josephi» in 1772 with either. **Not part of this reading:** the baptism and death books of 1784–1880 (M01069008–M01069314) and the status animarum; in the baptism book II M01068929 and M01068930 are two exposures of one opening, a tipped-in slip over part of the first (two certified copies of 1790 from the Cerovlje book). The readers' unsettled cells (the Baxa canon godfather of 2 July 1780, a faint entry of 25 June or July 1778 whose last word begins D-, the month of the death of Josephus) are named in their reports.

**Read on 11 November 2026: the Pazin baptism book of 1643 to October 1655 (FamilySearch 9R2C-ZNP, images 42–99; `doc` for the entries, `inf` where said).** The waypoint holds three books of the Pazin parish on the Zagreb microfilm: births 1582–1624 (images 2–38), **births 1645–1665 as the cover card calls it (image 40, «inv. br. I (167)»)** and births 1655–1689 (cover at image 99, «II (168)»). The book labelled 1645–1665 in fact holds **baptisms from 9 April 1643 to 12 October 1655** (the last, on a short torn leaf at image 92 right), a confraternity roll before and after (images 43–46, and «sub Anno 1656» at 93–94), and an end-of-item card at image 96; the baptisms of the 1655–1665 years are in the next book, not walked. A reader walked every opening, 42–99, at full size, and the cells of the Port family and every Fran- word were zoomed. **No Defranceschi in any form, in any role, in these twelve years** (Defranceschi, Defranceski, Defrančeski, Deffranceschi, Defranca, Defrancaschi, Defranceschy, Defrancesci, Defrancheski, Defranci, di Franceschi, de Franceschi, Franceschi, de S. Vincenti, Sanvicenti; Atlas `cover` exits 0 for the family). **The Hort of 1668 is a Port in 1648: `doc`, three baptisms, and the bride herself `inf`.** The surname the book writes is **Port** (Port, port, once Porta), looped or open capital, the same P as in Patrini and Petrus in the same hand; no Hort, Horth or Kort stands in the book. **26 April 1648** (image 69, left page, entry 2 of 3; read at full size): the vicar general of Pazin, Petrus Gasprotich, «baptizavit **Joanna(m)** filiam ex legitimo thoro procreatam **Joannis Baptistae Port** conjugisque eius **Matthia**»; godparents D. Georgius, son of the late Ill. D. Petrus Gerardinus, lieutenant, and Domina Joanna, wife of the Most Excellent Dom. Franciscus Tranquilio, vicar of Pisino. **28 October 1649** (image 73 left, entry 3 of 4): **Adriana**, daughter of «Jo: Baptistae Port» and Matthia, godparents D. **Fabritius Rappitius** and D. Hellena, daughter of the late D. Nicolaus [Milosich]. **19 October 1651** (image 78 left, entry 1 of 5): **Gaspar**, son of «Dom. Gio: Batiste port» and Matthia, godparents Dionysius Geraldinus and Magdalena Grubischa. No other child of the couple in 1643–55, and no death of Joannes Baptista Port in the book. He is styled Dominus and Magnificus; he stands godfather in eleven cells (the first on 12 April 1643, the last on 25 January 1655), and his wife godmother in some fifteen (once, on 13 February 1652, the wife is written Andriana; Matthia is the last, on 6 June 1655, still «uxor Joannis Baptistae Port»). **inf:** the Joanna of 1648 is the bride of the Pazin marriage of 18 June 1668: the father has the same two names, he is dead («q.m») by 1668, she would be twenty, and **one of the two witnesses of 1668, read «D. Fabricio Rapiti(?)», is the Fabritius Rappitius who stood godfather to her sister in 1649**. The spelling differs: the 1668 cell is read **Hort** (a small initial with an ascender loop; on 11 November 2026 it was set against the same entry's own capital P of «Presbiter» and the h of «huius» and «adhibitis» at level 13: it has the h shape, not his P, so the reading Hort stands), the baptisms Port; no claim is made that either reading corrects the other, and the family is the Port of the baptisms. So Andreas Defranceschi of S. Vincenti (1668) took as his wife a daughter of a Pazin family of some standing, with a judge in it: **Gaspar Port, Judex, with a wife Adriana, stands in some twenty cells of 1643–48**, and a **Jacobus Port with Catharina** has a son baptised on 9 June 1654 (image 88 left); a Franciscus (?) Port, father of a Joannes Jacobus, 27 January 1644 (image 53 left, the initial smudged). How these Port men are related to Joannes Baptista is not written. The Port cells of the burial book (a Franciscus Port, about 31, buried 5 June 1668; an Antonius, son of the late Franciscus Port, 1669) are not joined to them. **Not settled:** the faded entries of July and December 1651 (images 77 left, 78 right), the wife's name in a cell of 1647 (image 66 left, «Por[…]» under a curled corner) and of 19 March 1652 (image 80 left), the godmother of 10 December 1651, the pale title line at image 83 right, and a few cells read at the size of the whole page; two of the scribe's year-digits are wrong in the book itself (1643 after 1645 on one folio, 1640 on another). Near-names read and not counted: Francinich (a judge Matthaeus), Franceschina and Constanza (given names), Pertz, Trost/Frost, Kalaz/Kalat, Flangini, Fratis. **Not read here:** the 1582–1624 book. The baptisms of 1655–1685 (book II) are read below. The book is not claimed as walked for every family: the unsettled cells are named in the search log.

**Read on 11 November 2026: the Pazin baptism book II, 4 April 1655 to 7 June 1685 (FamilySearch 9R2C-ZNP, images 100–254; `doc` for the entries, `inf` where said).** The cover card at image 99 reads «Matična knjiga rođenih (1655–1689), II (168)»; image 101 is a second exposure of the title opening; the first baptism (folio 1) is at image 102 right; **the text ends on image 254 right, 7 June 1685**, on a ruled foot, and a card «to be continued on another roll» and the Item 9 slate follow (images 255–259: slates, an end-of-roll card, a test target, blank frames); the baptisms from June 1685 are on the next roll (9R2F-DPD, read in part on 10 November). A reader walked every opening at full size and zoomed every Port, Hort, Kort, Rap- and Fran- word. **Defranceschi: one cell in thirty years, the known one** (Defranceschi, Defranceski, Defrančeski, Deffranceschi, Defranca, Defrancaschi, Defranceschy, Defrancesci, Defrancheski, Defranci, di Franceschi, de Franceschi, Franceschi, de S. Vincenti, Sanvicenti; Atlas `cover` exits 0). **24 March 1684** (image 246 right, third entry; the priest Matthias Chavalloni): «baptizavi **Maria** filia legitima **Francisci de Franceschi** et uxoris eius **Marina**. Patrini fuerunt Hilarius Culinas et Jacoba eiusdem uxor.» The reading of 13 September («Celin[?]») is now Culinas (level 13); no place, no trade and no «ex Sanvicenti» in the entry. **No child of Andreas Defranceschi «de Sanvicenti» and Joanna Port is baptised at Pazin between their marriage of 18 June 1668 and June 1685, and no Sanvicenti cell stands in the book: if they had children they were baptised elsewhere, most likely at Svetvinčenat (worklist 306).** **The Port family, from the baptisms (`doc` unless said).** Joannes Baptista Port, styled Magnificus, is godfather in the book until October 1657, and **died before 19 December 1660, when «Joannem Baptistam filium legitimum Joannis Baptistae Port ac eius uxoris Mattiae, qui post mortem patris natus est»** was baptised (image 136 right, entry 1; godparents the parish priest of Old Pisino and Domina Catharina, daughter of Martinus Rampel). The children of the couple in the two books are Joanna (26 April 1648), Adriana (28 October 1649), Gaspar (19 October 1651), **Lucia** (22 August 1656, image 111 right, «filia … Magnifici D. Joannis Baptistae Port et Mattiae»), **Joannes Christophorus** (8 January 1658, image 121 right) and the posthumous Joannes Baptista (1660). The widow Matthia stands godmother again and again to 1666 (on 25 April 1662 as «Vid.a relicta q.m Baptistae Port»; on 9 April 1666 she baptises at home a daughter of Fabricius Rapicius in danger of death); **Adriana is godmother as «filia q.m Joan: Bap: Port» on 25 February 1669 and 23 March 1672**, so she is alive after Joanna's marriage; a third daughter's name on 25 September 1664 begins Pant- and is not read. **A second Port family, apart:** Franciscus Port and Maria have Joannes Andreas (11 February 1657), Matthea Adriana (23 February 1659), a Joanna (14 November 1662), Joannes (9 July 1665) and a child of 27 September 1666; the book never says whether Franciscus is Joannes Baptista's brother. The Joanna of 1662 is not the bride of 1668. **Port again in 1682–84:** a Joannes Baptista Port with a wife Mathia has Georgius (20 April 1683, image 240 left, the godfather Martinus Rapicij) and Catharina (6 August 1684, image 248 right), and he is godfather on 22 December 1682 and 5 March 1684. **inf:** he is the posthumous son of 1660, then twenty-two. The Jacoba who stands godmother in the Franceschi baptism of 1684 is the Jacoba, wife of Hilarius Culinas, who stands with him on 22 December 1682 (image 236 right); that is all the book says that joins the two. No Hort, Horth, Kort or Orth form is a surname in the book; Rosto/Rotto/Rosso is a separate family (Franciscus Rosso with a wife Joanna); a Hertich or Kertich on 6 May 1685 (initial H or K, second letter e) is not Hort. **The Rappitius (Rapicius, Rapitius) family**, to which the 1668 witness «Fabricio Rapiti(?)» belongs, is in the book in every year from 1655 to 1685: Dominus Fabritius (alive in 1675, dead by 1679) with Lucretia, a Domina Stella (daughter of the late Andreas, later wife of Joannes Baptista Tranquilli, 1683), Martinus with Margarita, Andreas; the Port and the Rappitius stand together at the font from 1649 to 1666 (the godparents of Adriana in 1649, of Lucia in 1656 and Joannes Christophorus in 1658 were Rappitius) and Matthia Port is godmother to Fabricius's daughter in 1666. **Not settled, none a Defranceschi:** faded cells at images 157–163 (1664–65), the first name of the third daughter above, the surname initial of a Franciscus Port or Kort of 1 March 1664, a Franciscus Po?s of 15 August 1665, the first name of Lucretia's late husband (22 April 1683), the Kortsc- byname at image 171 left (8 May 1667), a leaf's worth of Nov–Dec 1667 between images 172 right and 173 left and Mar–Apr 1670 between 180 right and 181 left (no leaf visibly missing), and several cells that break off or lack a sponsor's name. Near-names read and not counted: Francinich, Francovich, Franceschina and Franciscina (given names), Poris/Paris, Porech, Deforsi, Foscho, Kerdich. Taken with the baptisms of 1643–55 and the later volume, **the Pazin baptisms from 1643 to 1685 are now read, with the gaps and unsettled cells named in the search log**; they are not claimed as walked for every family. **Found on 11 November 2026:** the children are at Svetvinčenat (see [that page](/places/svetvincenat/)).

name: Pićan
lead: The diocese Gologorica and Gračišće belonged to — but not the custodian of their registers.
body: A tiny bishopric with an outsized place in Istrian church history; in the Middle Ages both ecclesiastical and secular power at Pićan lay with the Patriarchs of Aquileia. Its own registers run from 1664 and are almost entirely digitised. One Defranceschi family was counted here in 1945.

name: Poreč
lead: Where Camillo De Franceschi was born in 1868, and where his father published L'Istria in 1879.
body: The Gologorica branch reached Poreč before it reached Crikvenica. It is also the seat of the diocesan archive that holds the later registers for half the parishes in this study.

**Read on 13 November 2026: the Poreč baptism index, the F and D sections of items 5–12 (FamilySearch 9R2F-6YH, 198 images; `doc` for each entry quoted, `inf` where said).** The film is not one book but eight alphabetical indexes of the baptisms of Parenzo, the early ones sorted by given name inside each letter, the two last (1804–16 and 1815–39) with one line per child, «Surname Given di father e mother, n. [date] c. [folio]». **A family of the name, not in this archive until now: three entries in the index of 1815–39, all filed under F, all «di Giuseppe e Caterina».** «**de Franceschi Marco Franc° della Giuseppe, e Caterina n. 4 aprile 1828 c. 176**» (image 154, right page; level 13; the second given name and the word *della* not settled); «**Franceschi Francesco di Giuseppe, e Caterina n. p.mo Luglio 1829 c. 195**» (image 155, left; the middle digit of the year is written like a 1 and the day is struck over, so at index level the date was read from the order of the lines and the folios, which run 169, 176, 190, 195, 197, 219 and ought to rise with the years; the register itself settles it, see the paragraph that follows); «**De Franceschi Maria Eugenia di Giuseppe, e Caterina n. 11 7bre 1831 c. 22[?]**» (image 155, left; the folio's last digit runs into the gutter). **inf:** three children of one couple, in three years. The index gives no place, trade or surname of the mother; the entries themselves are in the baptism register at those folios, which was opened later the same day (next paragraph); nothing here ties them to the Seghetto branch of the historian Carlo de Franceschi (b. 1809) at Parenzo or to any line of this archive. Not counted: Francovich, Franca, Folin and the many given-name Franceschi (a foundling «Francesca Antonia», 1827). **Not found in D or F of items 5–10 or of 1804–16: any other Franceschi.** **The death index (9R2X-FMW, 70 images, labelled «kazalo 1657–1825»):** D and F read at page size, no Franceschi in any form; the reader reports that every entry it saw is a marriage («Surname, groom con bride, date», from 1662), so that the label and the contents disagree (the reader's observation, not rechecked here). **Not read:** every other letter, and a «De Franceschi» filed under another letter or under Di. The index is not a nil for the parish, and the baptism register itself is the next step.

**The three entries in the baptism register itself, 13 November 2026 (FamilySearch 9R2F-6T5, Parenzo births 1815–1839, 163 images; the page number written at the top of each page is the index's «c.», image 95 holds pages 176/177, image 104 pages 194/195, image 118 pages 222/223; `doc` as read, the father's and the mother's cells checked by me at level 13 on the saved zooms).** All three are one couple: **Joseph, Comes (a count) «de Franceschi», son of Marcus Antonius, nobilis** («Joseph Di Franceschi Co. filius Marci Antonii» in 1828, «Joseph Co[mes] nobilis de Franceschi Marci Antonii filius nobilis» in 1829, «Joseph Comes de Franceschi Marci Antonii filius nobilis» in 1831), and **Caterina, daughter of Franciscus** (civilis in 1829, nobilis in 1831). The mother's surname is written like *Dagun-/Jagunzi*, with «de» before it in 1831, and is **not settled**; neither is her father's second name in 1828. **4 April 1828, page 176, third entry:** born 4 April, 3 in the afternoon, baptised 17 April by the archpriest Petrus Predonzani; the cell names **two** children, «Marcus Franciscus et Joannes Baptista», so probably twins (the reader's reading; the second name is split over the line and the legitimacy cells carry dashes, not settled). **1 July 1829, page 195, first entry, house 76:** «Franciscus Bortolomeus Nicolaus», born 1 July, 5 in the morning, baptised **8 July 1829** (the year read at level 13), sponsors Antonius Cucavaz and Helena, a countess, the midwife Angela Vendramin, nobilis. The «1 July» of the index is therefore the birth, and the year is 1829. **24 September 1831, page 222, fifth entry:** «Maria Eugenia, Angela et Carolina», one girl with three names, born 11 September, 2 in the evening (the index's date), baptised 24 September (the reader's reading; the day is written lightly); sponsors Franciscus Corner and Carolina, wife of Antonius Cucavaz, of Venice. **inf:** a noble household of the town in the 1820s–30s, with Venetian sponsors, not a household of the Defranceschi of this archive; nothing in the three entries ties it to any of its lines, and Franceschi with the particle is a form the Atlas decides record by record. Looked at: images 80, 81, 95, 104, 118 and 120 as whole pages; images 82–94 and 121–131 as strips of the parents' columns only (no other Franceschi father, no child of this couple in 1826–27 or 1832–34 at that reading, which is **not** a walk of those pages). Not read: images 141–162 and pages 250–266.

name: Seget
lead: An estate south of Umag, bought in 1720 by a de Franceschi family two generations out of Crete.
body: Venice granted the land in 1604 to families fleeing Greece and Montenegro. Captain Vincenzo Cuchich of Šibenik sold it in 1623 to the Venier of Venice, who held it a century and made it a working estate. In 1720 Nicolò and Marc'Antonio de Franceschi, sons of Giorgio, bought all of Catarina Bernardo Venier's Istrian property; in 1730 Umag made them citizens, them and their heirs.

They had reached Istria fleeing Crete after the Candian War of 1669. A monograph on the estate records that the family had two branches in Istria — one at Gologorica, one at Umag and Seget — and that family archives survive from both. One De Franceschi household was still counted at Seghetto in the 1945 census.

name: Svetvinčenat
lead: The oldest De Franceschi household in Istria this archive can date: a baptism of 21 December 1628, thirty-eight years before the cluster everyone knew about.
body: **«Alì 21 Decembre — Elena fiola di Francescho di Franceschi et di Eufemia sua consorte fu batezata da me piovano sopra deto. Fu compare s.r Zan Piero Quelo. Comare Chiara consorte di Tomaso Ostricich.»** Svetvinčenat, Births 1589–1646, image 58, read off the film on 13 September 2026.

Until that morning this archive dated the family here from **1666** — Colotta in October, Fioretta in November, two children to the font in one autumn. The 1628 entry puts a whole household here a generation and a half earlier, with a wife, a daughter and two godparents out of the parish's own gentry. It is a settled family, not an arrival.

It also reorders Istria. The earliest dated occurrences ran Labin 1615, Moncalvo di Pisino 1661, Svetvinčenat 1666. They then ran Labin 1615, Svetvinčenat 1628, Moncalvo 1661; the Labin 1615 has since been withdrawn, and on 11 November 2026 godparent cells of the name were found in this parish's baptism book from 1605, so they now run **Svetvinčenat 1605, Rovinj 1619, Moncalvo 1661** — and the sentence this archive wrote about the family reaching Svetvinčenat five years after Moncalvo has it backwards by thirty-three.

It is not one entry, though: the 1589–1646 book's index carries **one** De Franceschi record in fifty-seven years, because an index carries children and not godparents, and read page by page on 11 November 2026 the book holds the name in some forty godparent cells from 1605 and two baptisms of a child (below); the 1568–1588 book and the 1581–1623 marriage book hold none by index and have not been read page by page. And nothing joins Francescho to the Nadal, Batta, Anto, Andrea and Gaspo of the 1660s and 70s — thirty-eight years is one long generation or two short ones, and no entry says which.

Across six of its nine parish books the parish yields **118 indexed records** of the name, from 1628 to 1887. Nineteen are marriages, eight of them daughters marrying out. One name recurs at both ends: a **Quelo** stands godfather in 1628, and a **Quelis** — Andriana, wife of the canon Ottavio — stands godmother to Nardo's son in 1707.

**Read on 11 November 2026: the Svetvinčenat baptism book 1663–1708 (FamilySearch 9R28-2JM, roll 86, images 5–206; `doc` for the entries, `inf` where said).** Image 5 is the inside of the cover on the left and folio 1 on the right (the first baptism is of September 1663); the last baptism is on image 197 right, **23 December 1708**; image 198 carries a later note (17 July 1812) handing the book, 191 written leaves, to the commune's mayor, and image 200 left a re-listing of baptisms of 1696–98 «registered in their place»; images 202–205 are the filming cards (the end-of-reel card names roll 87 as the continuation). Images 23, 49, 180 and 199 are second exposures of the opening before them. The language is Italian to 1672, Latin from 1674, mixed Latin and Italian under the archpriests Petrus Apostolus (1677–88) and Christophorus Apollonius (to about 1696, Italian), Latin again under the parish priest in 1695–98, then Italian under Lorenzo Osualdo (to January 1703) and Nicolo Summa. Two readers walked every opening at full size and zoomed every Fran-, De Fran- and Port/Hort word, and I read the cells for the first Giacomo (image 39), the second Jacobus (87), Victoria of 1681 (83) and Zuana of 1688 (107) myself at page size; the others stand on the readers' level-13 notes. The book is **not claimed as walked** for every family: faint entries on images 93–105 and a few others are named in the search log.

**Andreas Defranceschi, son of the late Jacobus, and Joanna: their children are here.** The Pazin marriage of 18 June 1668 gave «Andream filium q.m Jacobi Defranceschi … De Sanvicenti» and «Joannam filiam q. Joa: Bapt. Hort» (see [Pazin](/places/pazin/)); no baptism of theirs stands at Pazin. At Svetvinčenat the couple is not in the book at all until 1671. **23 October 1671** (image 39 left, first entry): «Giacomo fig.lo di S. Andrea de Franceschi, e D.a Zuanna sua legitima Consorte, nato sotto li 15 del corr.te», baptised by the canon Christophorus Apollonius; the compadri are a Zebelin woman and «la S.ra Marta mog.e del S. Antonio de Franceschi». **6 January 1674** (image 52 left, third entry): a daughter, born on the 2nd, of «Mr And.a di Franceschi e di Zuanna sua leg.ma Consorte» (the girl's first name begins P and is not settled). **13 March 1679** (image 76 left, fourth entry, Latin): a son, first name abbreviated «Jol.» and not settled, of «Andreae de Franceschi Joannaeq. ingalium». **Between 4 and 6 February 1683** (image 87 right, fifth entry, Latin): «**Jacobus** filius legit. et nat. **Andreae de Franceschi q.m Jacobi**, et **Joannae** ingalium», godparents Vincentius Calimeni and a Julia Quelij, baptised by Petrus Apostolus by the parish priest's licence. That entry is the tie: the father is again «q.m Jacobi», the mother Joanna, and the boy is named for the grandfather. `inf` (strong): this is the couple married at Pazin in 1668, so Joanna Port of 1648 has a family here. The first Giacomo of 1671 and the second Jacobus of 1683 carry the same name, so the first probably died young (`inf`); the archive's index record «Giacomo De Franceschi 1671» is very probably his baptism (`inf`, the index gives no parents). **The couple at the font:** «Andrea atque Joanna ingales de Franceschi» godparents on 13 Cal. Sept. 1679 (77 left); «Joanna uxor Andreae de Franceschi» on 2 Cal. Oct. 1680 (80 left); «Andrea de Franceschi, et Joanna Binesich» in 1681–82 (82 left, 85 left; the second word is the same on both and not settled); «Andrea de Franceschi f.i Jacobi» godfather in 1683 (89 right), and **«D.a Zuana moglie di Andrea de Franceschi»** in 1690, 1691 and 1692 (118, 122, 128), «Joanna uxor And.ae de Franceschi» on 20 May 1696 (137 right). Zuana and Joanna are the clerk's Italian and Latin for one woman's name. **His death.** «Margarita filia And.ae de Franceschi» is godmother on 22 May 1696 (137 right, third entry) and **«Margarita figlia del q.m Andrea de Fran.ci» on 3 April 1697** (139 right): an Andrea de Franceschi was dead by then; and **«Dna Zuana moglie del q.m Andrea de Francesz-/chi»** is godmother on 15 April 1706 (181 right). If these are one man, Andreas died between 22 May 1696 and 3 April 1697 and his widow Zuana lived to 1706 (`inf`; the readers could not say which Andrea is Margarita's father, and the 1706 widow's husband is not given a father). **Not his:** «Flora figla de m.r Andrea da Franceschi, e di D.a Mattia sua leg.ma cons.» (c. 10 September 1692, 127 left, sixth entry) has a wife called Mattia, and on 5 Nones March 1683 «Victorius» is the son of «Andreae de Franceschi f.i?/q.m Mathei, et Mathaeae?» (88 right, fifth entry): a **second Andrea de Franceschi, son of a Matthias, with a wife Mattia** (`inf`), not Joanna's husband. A third, «Andreas Frances[chi]» with a Dominica, has a son Gaspar on 14 July 1675 (60 left). Andreas himself, born before 1650, is not in a book that begins in 1663; no entry of Jacobus's death is in it.

**Gaspar, the other son of Jacobus: the Casparus of 1708 is here.** «Gasparis de Franceschi f.i/q.m Jacobi» is the father of the twin girls Antonia and Joanna baptised 12 Cal. Martii 1683 (88 left, sixth entry) and of Victoria of 4 Idus Maii 1684 (91 left, seventh entry; the mother's first name is not settled); the earlier children are Andreas (born 14 November 1677, 71 left, third entry; mother Maria) and **Victoria, born in December 1681** (83 right, last entry: «filia Gasparis de Fran-/cesdi, atque Mariae ingalium», godparents Marino Fecca and «Dom.a uxor Baptistae de Franceschi»). Two Victorias in three years means the first probably died (`inf`). From July 1688 the wife is **Antonia**, never Maria: «Zuana figlia di m.r Gasparo de Franceschi et di Ant.a sua legg.ma consorte, li 26 Giun.» (1 July 1688, 107 right, third entry, compari Martin Stancovich and «Marina figlia del q.m Batta de Franceschi»), Andriana (28 November 1689, 115 right), Batista (4 April 1692, 125 right), Jacobus (1 November 1696, 138 right), Veneranda (March 1701), and Giacomo, born 5 September 1706 (182 right). He is godfather in two dozen cells from 1689 to 1707, the last in February 1707. **Inference** (`inf`): a widower Gaspar married Antonia between 1684 and 1688 (the marriage books of those years are not on FamilySearch; the 1581–1623 and 1762–1895 marriage books do not reach them), or there were two men of the name; and **the Casparus de Franceschi «ex Sanvicenti» who stood godparent with his daughter Victoria at Pazin on 31 July 1708 is this Gaspar**, the only one in the town's book, with a Victoria of twenty-four or twenty-seven years (the cell says only «eius filia»). Andreas and Gaspar are both «q.m Jacobi»; they are very probably brothers (`inf`), sons of the Jacobus Defranceschi who was dead by 1668.

**The other houses in the book, with the fathers the clerk gives them (`doc`, readers' level 13).** **Antonius, «q. Mattio»**, with Marta: Franceschina (23 October 1667, 13 left), Mattia (11 November 1669, 26 right), Maria (2 September 1681, 82 right); Marta is godmother in some forty cells in 1666–88 and again to 1693, and on 20 August 1689 a Mattio is «fig. del q. Anto de Franceschi» (113 left); a «Franc.o de Franceschi quondam Mattio» is godfather on 5 April 1667 (11 left), so two men of the name are called sons of a Mattio. **Batta and Domenica** (Fioretta 1666, Marina 1669); Domenica is «Menega … r.ta del q.m mistro Batta» by 1689, and **Piero, «q. Batta»**, with Vittoria has Joanna Baptista (27 January 1696, 137 left), Nadal (2 February 1698, 142 right), Domenica (4 November 1703, 166 right) and Domenica again (10 May 1705, 175 left): the Piero and Vittoria of the 1710 baptism of Marina are very probably these (`inf`). **Nadal and Fiora** (Colotta, 24 October 1666, 8 right). **Leonardo, Lunardo or Nardo**, with Maddalena (Vittoria, 1693; Raymundus, 31 August 1699) and, from 1702, Eufemia (Piero, September 1707): the Nardo of the 1707–09 entries already on this page is the same man by name (`inf`). **Matthaeus, «q.m Antonio»** (136 left, 25 July 1695), with Joanna «concubina» (Joannes, 1695; Maria, 1695), a Joanna of Gallignana «concubina publica» (Vittoria, October 1696), a son Caesar «illegitimus» (1 January 1700), and from 1701 a wife (Eufemia Marta; Antonio, 11 February 1704, with Zuana). Two priests of the name, one «Pre Bertuzzi de Franceschi da Dignano» (1688–89) and a «P. Mattio de Franceschi» (1689, 1693), baptise by licence; nothing says they are of these houses. The patronymics matter: **the book names Jacobus, Mattio, Batta and Antonio as fathers, and nobody before 1663 for any of them**, so the Francescho de Franceschi of the 1628 entry still does not join them.

**What is not in the book, and what was not counted.** No Franciscus de Franceschi with a Marina, the Pazin couple of 24 March 1684, in any role; no Port in the book; Mattio «dall'Hort», a tailor with a wife Pasqua (1663–73), and the later «dell'Orto» family and priests are a local name «of the garden» and are not counted as Joanna's Pazin Port (the Pazin marriage cell reads Hort, an h and not that scribe's P, so the marriage clerk wrote Hort where the baptism clerk wrote Port). Terms tried: Defranceschi, Defranceski, Defrančeski, Deffranceschi, Defranca, Defrancaschi, Defranceschy, Defrancesci, Defrancheski, Defranci, di Franceschi, Franceski, the leads and Franceschi (every form of the Atlas's catalogue, `cover` exit 0; the book writes de, di and da Franceschi, in Latin also de Franceschis), Port, Porta, Hort, Horth, Kort, Kortich, Kertich, Orth, Rappitius. **Near-names, read and not counted:** the Francaz, Franaz, Franciaz and Crasenaz family, Franconich, Francinich, Franković, «Franciscovi[ch]» of 1688, Bergamo, Moscarda, Mantica, Muscarda, and Franceschina and Francesca as given names. **Not settled:** the first names of the daughter of 1674 and the child of 1679; the mother of Victoria 1684; the patronymic before «Nattale» (87 right, sixth entry) and before «Mathei» (88 right); «Andrea» or «Antonio» as godfather on 11 January 1671 (34 left); the abbreviated Fran.ci cells on 123 left, 124 right and 143 right; the faint entries of 99–105.

**Read on 11 November 2026: the Svetvinčenat baptism book 1589–1646 (FamilySearch 9R28-K6X, roll 86 item 3, images 4–170; `doc` for the entries, `inf` and `lead` where said).** The book is not in date order: it is **filed by the first letter of the child's given name, in runs that each start again in 1589** (A 4–16, B, C, D, E, F 50–58, G 60–72, J 72–80, L from 81, M 89–106, O from 109, P 115–119, S 127–129, T 133–136, V 138–145, Z 146–155), with late additions of 1611–33 and a few of 1640–46 at the end of the runs and a last appendix of late additions from image 156; the opening slate calls it «1589–1631». Latin to about 1603, Italian after. Images 168–170 are blank or back-board scribbles, 171 the end-of-item card of roll 86. Two readers walked every opening at full size and zoomed every Fran- word; I read the baptism of 1627 below myself at page size. **Pages with no recoverable text:** both pages of images 137, the left of 146, the right of 157 and 167 (faded, or set off from the facing page): a cell cannot be excluded there. The earlier reading of this book, by its index, is re-found: the baptism of 21 December 1628 is on image 57 right.

**The name is in this book from 1605, in about forty godparent cells, always written «di Franceschi», never De-.** It stands at other people's fonts and is in no index, which carries children only. **Tomaso, styled «cavalier»,** with Fumia (Eufemia), wife of Polo Vodopia, as co-godparent each time: an abbreviated «Fr.ci» cell of 1591 (image 82 left), a Latin cell of about 1604 (27 right), **30 May 1605** (28 left, «compare Tomaso d. Franceschi cavalier», all letters legible) and 2 July 1607 (69 left). **Zuane:** 23 March 1606 (48 left), 5 February 1609 (10 right), 17 March 1616 (161 right, «Zuane de franceschi», complete) and two cells of 1614 and 1616 whose ending is lost (148 right, 149 right). **Piero:** 6 March 1613 (53 left), 14 May 1614 (87 left), 17 February 1613 (142 right, «Piero de Franceschi et Andriola moglie di Mattio da Monfalcone»), 8 May 1622 (79 left), October 1624 (121 right), and in 1629–32 five more (123 left, 126 left, 135 right, 145 left, 154 left); on **9 June 1630** he is «misko Piero di Franceschi da Chrugna» (154 left) and on 22 November 1629 and 7 July 1632 the word after his name reads «Chovgnel» or «chougnel», and in January 1631 «mistro Matio di Franceschi chargnel?» (14 right): letters not settled, but **a Carnian by-name (Cargna, Cargnel) is possible for the men of the name here (`lead`)**, in a parish the archive already knows the Carnians settled. **Francesco and Eufemia («Fumia»):** godfather 3 March 1624 (36 right) and 11 February 1626 (56 left, with Fumia his wife), and then **two baptisms of their daughters: Maria, 9 March 1627** (114 right, «Maria figliola di m.ro Fran.co di Fran.ti», the surname abbreviated, the mother's name read by the readers as Eufemia, godfather Gio. Pietro Quellis) **and Elena, 21 December 1628** (57 right, the entry already told above); he stands godfather in some fifteen more cells to 1632 (with Fumia as godmother on 1 January 1632 and 16 November 1631). **Antonio:** 27 March 1630 (80 left); **Matio** son of Piero is godfather in February 1629 (57 right, «Matio fiolo di m.ro piero di Franceschi»); **Filippo** c. 1611–13 (168 left); and **«m.ro Giac.o di Franceschi» on 25 October 1646** (58 right, the forename abbreviated), the only Giacomo of the name in the book and the last entry that carries it.

**What this does and does not settle.** **No Jacobus, Andreas or Gaspar de Franceschi is named as a father in the book, and no baptism of Andreas or Gaspar is in it** (the runs A and G, and J for Jacobus, were read): the sons of the late Jacobus who married and had children in 1668–1706 were born after the last entry of this book (October 1646) and before the next one begins (September 1663), or elsewhere; **no baptism book of Svetvinčenat for 1647–1662 is on the film** (`inf`, from the catalogue's list: births 1568–1588, 1589–1646, 1663–1708, 1709–1764, 1764–1791). The Giacomo of 25 October 1646 is a `lead` for Jacobus: alive as a godfather in 1646 and dead by 1668, he would fit the father of a son born in the years that no book holds; the cell gives no more than the abbreviated forename and the surname. A cell of 24 July 1605 (85 right, «m.r Giacomo d. Fran-/ces.») breaks at the line end and does not say -chi or -co, and a Francesco son of the late Giacomo, a weaver «in S. Vicenti» (88 right, 29 July 1613, the surname «Fra?a»), is not counted. **The names of the generations are the names of the households of 1663–1708** (Piero, Mattio, Antonio, Francesco, Giacomo), and one of them, «Ant.o di Franceschi di Piero» (25 October 1667, read in September, not settled by the later readers), would make Piero of 1609–32 a father of the 1660s Antonio; no entry says so and **no descent is claimed** (`lead`). Not found: no De-, Defranca-, Defranci- or Defranceschi spelling, no Port or Hort. **Near-names, read and not counted:** Francaz, Franchaz, Francal and Francacio (a family: Antonio, Vicenzo, Pasqual, Bastian), Franchin, Francolin, Francin, Franelin, Fioli and Calimeni, Franceschina and Francesca as given names, the friar Fra Gregorio, Francesco as a given name (Tagliapietra, Comino, Quirini, Rotta, Corelli). **Not settled:** the forenames of three Pieros or Zuanes (10 left, 50 left, 69 right), the letters of «Fran-» on 71 right (September 1613, «Piero di [g/F]ranuchi Cargnele Zoppo», probably Piero), 130 left, 142 left and 161 right (endings -cesco, -soli), and the Cargna readings above.

**Correction, 11 November 2026.** This page, the family page and the Rovinj page said that the 1628 baptism was the only sighting of the name in this book («one De Franceschi record in fifty-seven years») and that the baptism of 1628 ranked next after the Rovinj burial of 1619 among the dated Istrian records. That was true of the book's index and wrong of the book: read page by page it holds the name in godparent cells from 1605 and a child in 1627. The earliest dated Istrian cell of the surname is now the Svetvinčenat entry of 30 May 1605 (with abbreviated cells of 1591 and about 1604 before it); the Rovinj burial of 1619 and the baptisms of 1627–28 follow. The statements are corrected on [the family page](/lines/) and [the Rovinj page](/places/rovinj/) and logged on [the corrections page](/corrections/).

**Read on 11 November 2026, page by page: the Svetvinčenat baptism book 1709–1764 (FamilySearch 9R2H-RM8, roll 87, 214 images; `doc` for the entries, `inf` where said).** Until today this archive knew the book from its back index and from a hand-reading of about seventy images in September (the Defranceschi cells of 1737–1752 and a few leaves either side). **Every opening of the book has now been looked at**, by two readers in turn (images 5–109, 1709 to 7 October 1736; images 110–213, to February 1764), each page at full size and every word beginning De-, Di- or Fran- zoomed at level 13; the cells quoted below are the readers' level-13 notes, and I looked myself at the plate of the twins of 26 December 1737, of 26 March 1752 and of 24 November–1 December 1743. **The layout.** Images 5–8 are the filming card, the cover (pencil «1709–1763»; the archive's label says 1703) and the inside covers; the title page (image 9 right) is dated 17 February 1703 under the archpriest Nicolaus Summa, and the first baptisms on it are of January 1709. Latin and Italian alternate (Italian under Summa and the archpriests Salambat, Quelis and Batilico to 1736, Latin under Matthias Jedreicich from May 1736, Italian again from 1760 under Zadro). **From image 193 right the book is a back index by the child's first initial**, «child di father surname, date, @ folio», for the baptisms of 1709 to February 1736 (to image 211 left), with the baptisms of 1763–64 written into its blank spaces; a certificate on image 211 left, of 17 June 1812, hands the book to the mayor of Sanvicenti as 195 written leaves, beginning 17 February 1703 and ending **10 February 1764**; the last dated baptism the reader saw is 20 February 1764 (199 right), which does not fit that day and was not rechecked. Second exposures (112 = 111, 120 = 119, 125 = 124, 140 = 139, 153 = 152, 29 = 28, 47 = 46) were read as one opening and not counted twice; a loose slip lies over 152 right, and a loose marriage licence of 1819 over the back leaves (image 212).
