The book is **not claimed as walked**: the cells the readers could not settle are listed below, the ink fades badly on images 27–28 and 99–105, and the index scribe compresses the surname to «Defran-…-i», so its middle letters were not resolved one by one.

**1709–1736, the first half, which no one had read before (`doc`, level 13, with `inf` where said).** The name is in the book from the first year, and almost always at other people's fonts. **Francesco** is godfather on 21 March 1709 (11 left, fourth entry), **Gasparo** on 19 October 1709 (12 right) and 16 February 1711 (18 left; the surname's c squeezed). **Mattio**, styled «sig.r» and «D.o», is godfather on 24 December 1709 (13 right), 6 February 1710 (14 right), 15 April 1710 (15 right), 8 November 1711 (21 left, «Mattio de Franceschi **de Piero**»), early February 1714 (30 left) and on 6 October 1715 (33 right, «D.o Mattio di **Franchessi**»: the form is now in the Atlas catalogue as attested); he is not the Mattio q. Antonio of the 1695–1704 baptisms by anything written. **Piero and Vittoria**: Marina on 21 February 1710 (14 right, fourth entry, baptised by the archpriest himself, «per mano di me»), and **Battista** on 7 May 1712 (22 right, seventh entry, the surname abbreviated «Fran.i»; the back index files it as «Battista di Mro Piero, 7 Mag 1712 @ 14»): a son named for the grandfather, so Piero, son of Batta, of the 1696–1705 baptisms is very probably the father (`inf`). **Nardo (Leonardo), «mistro»**, and Zuanna: Zuanna wife of «mis.r Lunardo [de] Franceschi» is godmother in March 1710 (15 left, fourth entry, a blot where the *de* would stand); **Maria** of «Mis.r Pavlo de Franceschi, et di Zuanna», 13 August 1709 (12 left, first entry: the first letter of the forename reads P at level 13, and the back index files the same day under «Maria di Mro **Naido**»: very probably Nardo, `inf`); «**mistro Nardo di Franceschi** et D.a Zuanna» have Mattio on about 7–11 May 1713 (27 left, third entry), and **Zuanna, «v.ra del q.m Nardo di Franceschi», is godmother on 29 December 1713** (28 right, last entry; the same cell re-found on the second exposure, image 29), on 30 January 1714, 1 February 1714 and 15 April 1714 (30 left, 30 right). So Nardo died between May and the end of December 1713 (`inf`, from the «q.m»). **Giacomo and Batta, «quondam Gasparo».** «Batta de Fran.co **q.m Gasparo**» is godfather on 8 November 1725 (67 right), 5 November 1728 (79 right) and again in 1731 (85 right: «Batista di Franceschi»); «Giacomo de Fran.ci **q.m Gazparo**» is godfather in August 1728 (77 right) and «Giacomo Defranceschi q. Gasparo» on 5 March 1734 (96 left). **The only Gasparo of the family in the 1663–1708 book is [Gaspar q.m Jacobi](/person/gaspar-defranceschi-sanvicenti-q-jacobi/), father of Batista (1692), Jacobus (1696) and Giacomo (1706), alive to February 1707; a Gasparo dead by 1725 who had a Batta and a Giacomo is very probably he, and the Domenico Gasparo of 9 April 1731 is a grandson named for him (`inf`).** The book never names Gasparo's own father. **Batta** and «Anzola» (Angoletta) are godparents on 28 February 1716 (33 right, «Bat.a Franeschi»), have Martin on 17 November 1724 (65, «di Batta de Fran.ci e di Angoletta sua consorte») and Catta on about 10 February 1728 (75). **Gio Batta and Maria**: Battistina, born 18 November 1731 (88 left, first entry, «del S.r Gio: Battista de Fran.ci et di Maria»), whose mother the index file for her father gave as Anzoletta; and from March 1732 «**Maria v.q. Gio Batta Defranceschi**» is a godmother six times to December 1734 (89 right, 92 left, 93 right, 96 right, 99 left, 100 right), so a Gio Batta died between 18 November 1731 and March 1732 (`inf`). Whether Batta with Angoletta and Gio Batta with Maria are one man remarried or two is not settled. **Nadal, «m.ro»**, and Antonia: Vittoria (27 October 1723, 61 left), Pietro (baptised about 8 November 1725, 67 right), Gio Batta (about 17 September 1728, 79 left), Maria (March 1732, 89 right: «di Nadal de Franceschi et di Maria Antonia»), Pietro again (born 31 January, baptised 2 February 1734, 95 right, «Nadal de Fran-/ceschi e da Anta sua Legitima Consorte»); the two Pieros suggest the first died (`inf`). **Giacomo**: Domenico Gasparo, 9 April 1731 (85 right, third entry, «figlio di Giacomo de Franceschi quondam Gasparo, e di Donna Maria»); **Giacomo, 13 June 1731 (86 left, sixth entry, «di Sig. Giacomo de Franceschi et d'Elena sua Consorte»)** and «Elena mog.e di m.ro Giacomo de Franceschi» on 7 October 1731: **two wives in eight weeks, so two men of the name or a clerk's slip**; **Maria**, 4 November 1733 (94 right, first entry, «e di Antoletta»); «Antoletta mogie di Giacomo Defranceschi» is godmother on 29 September 1735 (104 right); and **Gasparo Zuane, born and baptised 9 April 1736 (108 right, fifth entry, «da Giacomo de Franceschi et di Dna Angola … ambi di questo Castello»), a baptism that is in no index, because the back index stops in February 1736 and the online index does not hold it.** Angola and the Angela of the twins of 1737 are one woman (the same scribe's g). **Pietro Defranceschi q. Lonardo** stands godfather on 12 December 1735 (106 left) and, with the by-name «Cagnelli» after Lonardo and a mark that may be a q., on 28 December 1735 (106 right): **the son of the Nardo who died in 1713, very probably the Piero of 1707, and so very probably the Pietro with Jacoba of 1738 (`inf`, three links)**; «Cagnelli» is the by-name the book gives a family of godparents («Giacomo Zanca Cargnello/Caynelli», 1731–36), and that is the Carnian by-name; it is a `lead`, not a descent. Eight more Defranceschi-type cells of the 1709–1736 half are in the readers' notes; none names a Jacobus or a Casparus as a father.

**1736–1764, the second half, and what it settles in September's reading (`doc` unless marked).** **The twins of 26 December 1737 (115 left, fifth entry) are Caspar and Antonius.** The archive's September transcription read the first name «[Cesare?]» and took *Caspar* from the index; at level 13 the word is **Caspar**, underlined as the clerk underlines a name, and the second «Antonij»; the parents are «Jacobo de Franceschi, et Angela eius legitima uxore» (the clerk writes it Anzola), godparents unchanged. **That makes the Gasparo of the twins `doc` and no longer `inf`**, and shows that the Gasparo Zuane of 9 April 1736, born to the same parents, was dead by December 1737, the name being given again (`inf`). **The Casparus of 15 June 1743 (133 right, first entry of page 119)** is read the same way as on 28 September: «Casparus filius legitimus Jacobi Defranceschi, et Pascasia ejus legitimae uxoris, amborum ex hac Parochia». **What this walk does not settle: the wife of «Jacobi Defranceschi».** The second reader wrote *Pascosia* or *Pascasia* wherever a Jacobus Defranceschi's wife is named in 1743–1759, on the assumption of a single wife; **I read two of those cells at the plate and they do not say it.** The godmother of 26 March 1752 (160 left, third line) is «Joannes Valentich, et **Franca / Marcario** uxor Jacobi Defranceschi» (the line breaks after *Franca*), and 17 December 1752 reads *Francisca*; the 1 December 1743 cell (134 left) is faint and ends «…cario uxor Jacobi Defranceschi». **So the archive's reading of two women, Pascasia and Francisca Marcario, stands, and nothing in this walk weakens or strengthens the argument for two men.** The walk's *Pascosia* readings are not used for that argument. **What the second half adds, and one reading not adopted.** The second reader wrote the husband of Jacoba as «**Fabro**» or «Fabri» (and so the father of Valentinus, 17 February 1745, Victoria, 10 February 1746, Euphemia, 17 September 1749, and the Jacoba of 1738–1746), a forename no other book of the castle has; **the archive reads Petri, Pietro, with Jacoba from the joint entry of 1738 and files those children under Pietro.** On 134 left (the entry that ends «et Jacoba uxor …atri Defranceschi») the first letter has the tall flourished capital of the same line's «Patrini», not an F; I could not settle it further, so **no Fabro household is told and the walk's Fabro is not adopted**. Victorius and Dominica (1745–1749) and Matthaeus and Francisca (1741–1752) are the households the September pages already carry, and no new house appears. **Caspar and Maria** («Maria uxor Caspari Defranceschi») stand as godmother several times in 1744–1749; **«Pasqua moglie di Mr Gasparo de Franceschi»** is godmother in the Italian entries of 1760–1764, six times named as Gasparo's wife (180 left, 184 left, 188 left, 197 left, 198 right twice) and once as «moglie di Mr **Giacomo**» (1 January 1762, 186 right), which the archive's September pages already read as one household; **«Gasparo figlio di Mr Giacomo de Franceschi»** is godfather on 1 August, 22 September, 11 October and 8 December 1762 (190 left to 191 left) and «Dn Gasparo de Franceschi di Giacomo» on 9 February 1764 (199 right), the last Defranceschi-type cell of the book; «Mr Giacomo de Franceschi» is godparent in July 1763 (195 left). The book ends before the test the 1765 marriage entry set (a living Giacomo after 22 October 1765), so it cannot make it. From 1759 the entries are in a new hand (Stancovich, from 177 right, 26 September 1759) and then Italian; the surname is written *de Franceschi* in both.

**What is not in the book, and what was not counted.** **The book names no Jacobus or Casparus as a father before 1737**: the Jacobus of 1683 (Andreas's) and of 1696 (Gaspar's) are not at any font as a man named so before the Giacomo of 1728, and **which of the Giacomos of 1728–1736 is Gaspar's son of 1706 (or of 1696) is not settled by this book**; none of Kovačina or Kalanj was met in either half (the readers noted them only if seen, their forms were not typed to them, and no nil is claimed), and no Port or Hort. **Terms**: the readers took every word beginning De-, Di- or Fran-; the forms they met are Defranceschi, de and di Franceschi, Defranceski (131 right, 136 left, 147 right, 164 right), «Del. Franceschi» (131 right), **Francetchi** (1729–33, Atlas: attested already), **Franchessi** (1715, now attested), «Franeschi» and «Defraneschi» (the c thin or joined), and the index's compressed «Defran-…-i» (the Atlas's `cover` for the surname exits 0 on every form of the family). **Near-names, read and not counted:** the **Francaz** family (Pasqual, Bortolo, Vicenzo the canon), Franaz and Franeaz, Franciaz, **Coffranaz**, **Franceschina** and **Francesca** as given names (the widow of Mattio Stancovich), Francesco as a given name (Mandica, Moscarda, Manzoni, Bergamo, Climeri), Franeinich, Francovich, Frattoni and Frassoni (the chancellor and a canon), Rafoni, «Piero Ban» (read twice at level 13 as Ban); **a Gerolimo (Girolamo Maria) Franceschi, «Agente» of the lord of the castle, with a wife Andriana, in about thirty cells of 1722–1732, is not counted**: the book calls him «Sig.r» and the lord's agent, and ties him to no other house here, though **Vittoria, widow of «Cosmo de Franceschi»** (1725–1732, the daughter of Bortolo Francaz) stands in the same cells and is not tied to him either. «Defuncti» (the Latin) was read as Defranchi in three places and zoomed: not a Defranceschi cell. **Not settled:** the forename of the father on 13 August 1709 (P or N, above); the first words on 110 left (seventh entry, father «S?ir»); a godmother's husband on 158 right (20 May 1751) beginning V or D and ending -ch, followed by «Fran…»; 159 right (13 February 1752, eleventh entry), «Baptista de …»; 129 left (14 January 1742), «Jacobus Def-r-a-n» with the rest lost at the leaf's edge; the word after Giacomo on 4 November 1733 (read Delpreo/Selpreo, perhaps a by-name); the date of the last entries against the certificate; and the middle letters of every cell of the back index.

**Read a second time on 12 November 2026: the Svetvinčenat baptism book 1764–1791 (FamilySearch 9R2H-PTL, roll 87, images 4–131; `doc` for the entries, `inf` where said).** The volume was read frame by frame in September (the six-baptism list and the households on the family page come from that reading); three readers have now taken every image again, each page at full size and every cell beginning De-, Di-, Da- or Fran- enlarged, and I looked myself at the plates of the cells quoted below. **The layout.** Image 4 left is a damaged flyleaf, 4 right the first text leaf (20 February 1764, Archpriest Simon Zadro); the last baptism is 4 May 1791 (129 right); 130 left holds a visitation note of 28 May 1791 and an Italian note of 17 June 1812 handing the book over (beginning 20 February 1764, ending 28 May 1791); 130 right is blank; 131 left is the end-of-item slate and **131 right the title slate of an «Item 2» with the same title and years (1764–1791), which is not on the folder and has not been opened.** Second exposures (27 = 26, 43 = 42, 89 = 88, 104 = 103, 116 = 115) were read as one opening. The written folio numbers jump from 32 (36 right) to 38 (37 right) with the dates running on, so cite image and side. The book is **not claimed as walked**: the readers list the cells they could not settle, a loose Italian slip hides one entry on 88 right (it reads in full on 89 right), and the left-page images lose about a hundred pixels at their right edge (images 4–46 were re-read stitched to their right pages; 47–131 were not). **What is new.** **1. Gasparo de Franceschi «q. Joannis Battae», with his wife Maria, 1767–1772 (`doc`).** About forty godparent cells from 15 June 1767 to 23 August 1772 name a Gasparo with a wife Maria; in three of them the clerk writes his father: «Maria uxor Gasparis de Franceschi q. Joannis Battae» (12 February 1769, 24 right, enlarged by me), the same in 9 March 1769 (25 right: «Antonio Defranceschi q.m Vitorio e Maria consorte di Dno Gasparo Defranceschi q.m Gio:Bata», both couples named together, enlarged by me) and «Gasparo de Franceschi q. Joannis Baptae» on 20 May 1769 (28 left). **So the Gasparo whose wife Maria stands at the fonts in these years has a father called Gio. Batta, and the roster's identification of Maria's husband as the son of the late Antonio (made by elimination, `inf`) cannot stand for him as it was written;** see the correction of today. Whether this Gasparo is the son of the Batta «q.m Gasparo» of 1716–31 (so a grandson of Gaspar q.m Jacobi) is `inf` on the name and the castle alone, no entry names both. **What is not settled:** the Italian entries of 1760–64 (the 1709–1764 book, above) call a «Mr Gasparo» the son of Giacomo, and a Gasparo with a wife **Pasqua** stands in this book in 1764–65 (5 right, 6 right, 7 right; his first name is doubtful in the first two, «Gaspa-ro» in the third); Pasqua and Maria may be two wives of one man or the wives of two men, and the father is Giacomo in one book and Gio. Batta in the other. No baptism of a child of Gasparo and Maria is in 4–131. **2. Antonio's father: «Antonio Defranceschi q.m Vitorio» (`doc`, 9 March 1769, enlarged by me; also «Antonio de Franceschi q. Vitorio» on 25 February, 5 July 1769 and others).** The Antonio of the castle (alive to 12 October 1788) is the son of a Vittorio, dead by 1769; his own son is the Vittorio of 1773, 1782–91, so the name runs Vittorio, Antonio, Vittorio. Whether Antonio's father is the Victorius with Dominica whose children are baptised 1745–49 (the twin Dominico of 1748 among them) is a `lead` only, nothing in this book says it. **3. Domenica's twin is found: Maria, baptised in danger of death on 21 January 1776 (57 right, first entry; `doc`, enlarged by me).** «Maria filia legitima gemina ad. Antonij Defranceschi ac Matthiae ejus conjugis, nata hac nocte elapsa. Baptizata ob imminens periculum … per Archip. Massalini», godmother Giacoba (a Cerolin), no godfather; the entry after it is Domenica's. The year is written 177-: 1776 comes from the run of dates on either side. **She may or may not be the «Maria filia Antonii» who is a godmother on 18 January 1786 and 30 September 1787 (she would be ten and eleven, young for a godmother): not identified.** **4. A second child of Vittorio and Euphemia: Maria, born 1 and baptised 2 October 1786 (113 right, enlarged by me; `doc`),** «Maria filia legitima ac naturalis Victori et Euphemiae jugalium De Franceschi, nata heri», godparents Joannes Volpe and Maria Elisabetha Bizzamano, wife of Joseph Basilisco, baptised by Joannes Venica. September's list had one baptism of the couple (Maria Matthia, 1784). **5. What the second reading does not change, and a reading not adopted.** The first reader took the entry of 22 December 1773 as twin girls, Pasqua and Vittoria; the line reads «Pasqua e Vittoria figlia di Giacomo de Franceschi e di Nicoletta giugali, nata a ore sedici…» (enlarged by me), **figlia and nata in the singular, so one child with a double name as the household list has it**, and the twins are not adopted. The entry of 7 March 1778 for Joannes, son of «Jacobi Defranceschi et Nicolae», godfather Antonius Defranceschi, is read here as the 7th and the roster has the 3rd (the number is followed by a superscript): **not settled, to be looked at again.** Nicolotta, Nicolina and Nicola are one woman (`inf`, the household is the one the marriage of 10 June 1772 makes). The rest of the family's appearances in the book are godparent cells: Antonius 25 December 1774 to 12 October 1788 (13 entries to August 1781 alone), Mattia his wife 1775–1788, Dominicus with Victoria (1772–76) and then with Fusca, Fosca, Jusca (from 1779, about thirty-five cells to 7 November 1789; the last Dominicus is 3 February 1790), Victorius and Euphemia to the last baptism of the book; none names a father's father or a village but Svetvinčenat. **What is not in the book:** no Hort, Port, Covaz or Covac in any role (the readers were asked for them by name; the Atlas's spellings were not typed to them, so no nil is claimed for those names), no Kovačina or Kalanj (not asked for). **Near-names, not counted:** the Carnian **Corva** (Corvia, Corvo, Corua) «ex Cargna» in some twenty cells, read at enlargement as ending -a and not Covaz; Cervar, Cruvilla, Cavano; Francesco and Franciscus only as given names (Fabris, Zuliani and others); **Francej/Francez** (15 left, 10 February 1767, a child's father, unsettled); the **De Fancea?** of 1 February 1787 (115 left, Petrus Apostolus, son of «Joannis Baptistae De Fancea?» and Maria: written without an r, doubtful, not counted); a **«vulgo Frances»** by-name (2 March 1787). Franceschini, Francovich, Franković, Franzin and Francin were not seen. Date gaps with no leaf missing: 28 April–25 May 1785, 28 June–24 July 1790, six weeks of August–September 1773. The hands: Zadro, Adamich, Zuppich, Massalini (1764–81), Luciani, Pittan, Fabris; from 7 March 1781 every entry is signed Andreas Tomljianovich, oeconomus parochialis; Conacich from 15 March 1782, Venica 1783–86 and from December 1787, Caneva registering from February 1787. Villages are named in the entries from 8 December 1787.

**Read on 12 November 2026: the baptism book of December 1815 to 26 June 1831 (FamilySearch 9R2H-PTL, the printed-table «Liber Baptizatorum IV», images 136–191, to page 112), for the Symphorosa of the Pazin entry of 1842.** Every image was looked at by readers; the cells quoted were enlarged by me, `doc`. **No girl is baptised Symphorosa or Sinforosa in these fifty-six images** (the one infant with the name is a second name of another family, 25 March 1827, not counted). **But the woman is in the book, as a mother: [Sinforosa de Franceschi](/who/sinforosa-defranceschi-volpi-campana/), "di Pietro" on 14 July 1828 and "fu Pietro" on 14 November 1829, wife of Giovanni Volpi, by-named Campana, son of the late Giovanni, a *civile*.** Her children: a son born 9 July 1828 (183 left, page 95, no. 42, Castello 34), a daughter born 6 November 1829 (186 right, page 102, no. 54, Castello 54), and a baptism at home in danger of death on 31 May 1831 (191 right, page 112, Latin: «Sinforosa de Franceschi defti Petri, civilis»; the father written there «Joannes … Volpi defti Joannis, civilis», without Campana; the child's name and the birth day are the reader's and doubtful). She is godmother six times, 1828 to June 1831, always as the wife of Gio. Volpi (Campana). **Her father Pietro** is dead by November 1829; a «Sig.r Pietro Defran-/ceschi» with a wife Anna is a godparent's husband on 23 March 1828 (182 right, page 94, no. 28), but the capital of *De* in that cell is doubtful, so the two are not joined (`inf`, if at all). **Is she the Symphorosa of Pazin in 1842, called *vulgo Campana*?** `inf`, probably: the same name (Latin in one book, Italian in the other), the same town, and the by-name *Campana* that the book gives her husband; against it, nothing met so far makes her a servant (*ancilla*) in 1842 when the book calls her a *civilis* wife in 1831, and the death of Giovanni Volpi has not been found. The MyHeritage row [Sinforosa Defranceschi (Volpi Campana)](/who/sinforosa-defranceschi-volpi-campana/) gives a birth year of 1829, which the book cannot support for a mother of 1828; it is left as it stands and flagged on its page. Her own baptism is not in this book: she was an adult by 1828, and the book of 1792–1814 is not on the Atlas's FamilySearch list. **The Castello 14 house** (the same book): a Defranceschi family whose father Domenico, the sacristan, is dead by 1825, and whose members appear as «fu Domenico»: Antonio, by-named Palosan (or Pelosan, the first letter is not always clear), husband of [Maria Bergamo](/who/maria-bergamo-defranceschi/), daughter of Giovanni, with Maria Maddalena (4 December 1825, 173 left), Gioanni Domenico (10 October 1828) and Domenica (25 October 1829) and godfather in eleven entries from 1827 to 1831; Maria, the midwife (*ostetrica*), written in the margin of almost every entry from January 1828 to June 1831, mother of Domenica Maria (20 July 1826, 176 left, father's cell empty); Benedetto, godfather on 1 September 1829; Francesca, mother of a Bergamo child born 21 June 1831 (191 right, «Francisca filia defti Dominici de franceschi»); and Giacoma, wife of Gio. Batta Crosilla Cusson (a carpenter or mason, Castello 52), mother of two children (January 1828, November 1830). The midwife Maria in Sinforosa's two entries is the same Maria Defranceschi fu Domenico, which is a reading of the margin, not a finding about kin: **nothing in the book says Sinforosa belongs to Domenico's house, or that either house is the Gologorica line or the earlier de Franceschi of S. Vincenti.** **Near-names, not counted:** *De Fiorencis*/Fiorencis (the notary-doctor family, on almost every page, and at page scale it looks like *De Franceschi*), Fabris, Volpi without Campana, and an «Anna Bombo di Franceschi» (191 left, 27 March 1831: no *De*, doubtful). Cells not settled: 180 left no. 55 (overwritten), 185 left no. 23 and 185 right nos. 33–35 (faint), 187 right no. 10, 189 right nos. 63–64 (overwritten), and a few godparents read at page scale only; no image was missing. The 1792–1814 births and the marriage and death books of the period were not read.

name: Umag
lead: The hamlet of Seghetto held one De Franceschi family in 1945. Every one of Umag's 128 registers is digitised.
body: The only parish in this study with a complete digitisation — 128 of 128 books, marriages from 1602. Whatever is here can be read from anywhere.

name: Vižinada
lead: Twenty-three records from 1750, and the parish where the Kaštelir family's children were born.
body: Vižinada holds the name from **1750**, when a Mathæus De Franceschi «of Anton» is buried, and carries it to 1877 — twenty-three records of ours out of twenty-four indexed, across nine volumes opening in 1663.

It is one parish of three. **Francesco Napoleone De Franceschi was baptised here on 7 September 1818**, son of **Giulio and Maria Ceselin**; both father and son then appear in the Kaštelir register, and the next generation again at Tar. See Kaštelir for the household as a whole.

Vižinada also carries the parish of **Kaštelir** in its own books, which is why the death of Mathaeus De Franceschi in 1819 — the one entry this archive found on film 005497893 — is catalogued under Vižinada and took place at Castellier. That confusion cost a day in September and is worth keeping in view.
**And Vižinada is why Draguč looked real.** FamilySearch's place parameter returns the two parishes' record sets identically; Draguč's twenty-five entries were these.

name: Vodnjan
lead: Twelve Defranceschi families in 1945, and — since 9 September 2026 — five documented generations behind them. The best-attested cluster in southern Istria, read out of a register nobody has indexed.
body: The 1945 cadastre counts twelve Defranceschi families at Vodnjan, against two at Gologorica and one at Gračišće. For most of this archive's life that was all it knew, and the twelve households were listed as its second open question.

They are not open any more. The parish books of Dignano — FamilySearch catalogue item koha:963267 — hold baptisms from 1815, marriages 1815–1884 and deaths to 1893. The baptism register gives eight households between 1816 and 1865. **The marriage register has never been indexed by anybody**, and was read here opening by opening.

What came out of it: a line five generations deep, from a **Pietro** standing behind a marriage of the 1770s, through **Gio. Maria De Franceschi and Michiela Zambaletta**, to their children **Pietro, Cristoforo and Veniera** and the grandchildren married off in the 1820s. A **second, separate line** descending from a Domenico. **Four women of the name married out before the books open** — Domenica, Antonia Maria, Lucia and Veniera — recoverable only because their daughters' weddings named their mothers. And one household of three brothers, all «di Giuseppe»: **Don Stefano the priest**, who witnessed sixteen weddings under the parroco Giovanni Tromba, and **Pietro the ploughman and Cristoforo the weaver**, who signed the same book with a cross.

The town's church paperwork ran to the **Ordinariate of Pola**; the banns could be waived by the **Imperial-Royal Circle Captaincy**. Weddings involving Vodnjan people were also held at **Šišan** and **Svetvinčenat**, and a «Matt.o de Franceschi da Dignano» was buried at **Rovinj** in 1728 — the same formula, ninety-six years apart, naming the town only from outside it.

**And the town those households lived in is gone.** Forebears' surname counts for Vodnjan, as of 2014, give the ten commonest names as **Hrelja 208, Macan 146, Šverko 110, Drandić 96, Vitasović 96, Lukić 81, Červar 80, Bliznac 76, Diminić 76, Pereša 76** — one person in thirty-one at Vodnjan is a Hrelja. **Not one of the families this archive read out of the town's own registers is among them.** Not Francin, Malusà, Vellico, Gorlato, Giachin, Ferrarese, Demarin, Biasiol, Damiani, Zanghirella, Codacovich, Moscheni, Forlani or Tromba — the names that fill the baptisms, marriages and deaths of the 1810s to the 1840s, and that this site has spent weeks reading one entry at a time. And no Defranceschi. The 1945 cadastre counted **twelve Defranceschi families here**, the largest concentration anywhere. What the surname list records is the **esodo** — the departure of the Italian-speaking population of Istria after 1945 and the resettlement that followed — visible as an almost complete replacement of a town's family names inside a single lifetime. It is also the plainest answer to a question this archive keeps asking: why a surname documented in one town for five generations has almost no living trace there. The list is the ten commonest names only — an old surname surviving at rank fifteen would not show

body: Recorded in the 1945 cadastre as Ceppici di Pòrtole, in the Motovun judicial district.

name: Crikvenica
lead: Named for a church: the Pauline monastery of 1412, in the deed that first records the name.
body: Nikola IV Frankopan gave the monastery to the Pauline fathers on 14 August 1412. The order stayed four hundred years, until Joseph II dissolved it in 1786, and for that whole time it was Vinodol's school, pharmacy and library.

A harbour came in 1877, a bathing beach in 1888, the first hotel in 1891 — a Vinodol village that became an Austrian seaside resort inside one lifetime. The Gologorica branch reached here by way of Poreč.

registers.note: Župa Crikvenica, 1798–1908, filmed from the Croatian State Archives. The register begins twelve years after Joseph II dissolved the Pauline monastery that gave the town its name.

name: Rijeka
lead: The largest documented concentration of the surname anywhere in Croatia — 447 records, once Vitipolis is recognised for what it is.
body: The indexed church books give 225 records under Fiume, 178 under Vitipolis and 44 under Rijeka. They are the same city. Vitipolis is the Latin for the city of Saint Vitus — Rijeka's patron, and the saint its cathedral is named for — which is also what the German Sankt Veit am Flaum means. Read together they make Rijeka the single biggest cluster of this family in the country, larger than Pola, Poreč and Omiš combined.

This is where the received account puts three separate arrivals: Domenico from 1614, Valentino out of Carnia made a citizen in 1739, and Giovanni Battista from the County of Pazin around 1740. The registers show de Franceschi children being baptised here from 1626.

registers.note: 447 indexed records under three names for one city.

name: Senj
lead: An Uskok garrison on the Habsburg Military Frontier — never Italian, unlike Istria.
body: Taken over by the Habsburgs in 1522 as a state-controlled Militärgrenze, and from the 1530s the base of the Uskoks, the refugee raiders who fought the Ottomans and Venice until an agreement between Habsburg and Venice expelled them in 1617. The Nehaj fortress was built by the Uskok captain Ivan Lenković in 1558.
Records for Senj fall to the State Archives in Rijeka, whose remit covers Primorje-Gorski Kotar plus the city of Senj. That inventory is not yet mapped.

registers.note: The Kvarner gap is now partly closed. FamilySearch holds microfilm of the Senj parish registers 1734–1920 and of Sv. Juraj near Senj 1695–1868, filmed from the Croatian State Archives in Zagreb — plus an Austrian army field-hospital register for 1805–06. The DARI collection itself still has no published parish-level inventory.

name: Mione
lead: A hundred and thirty people at 710 metres — and the Italian end of a documented migration into Istria.
body: First written on 15 June 1185, when Odolrico called Gusetto, Strabo, and Vecellone, son-in-law of Giovanni da Mione, received concessions from Domenico, abbot of Moggio. An independent comune until 1871, now a frazione of Ovaro in the Canale di Gorto.

A stone above the village, at some 1,600 metres, carries Venetic inscriptions — this valley was a route long before it was a parish. From the parishes of Ovaro and Luincis a long series of weavers took the road into Istria; the documents become numerous in the seventeenth century and frequent in the eighteenth.

registers.note: Confirmed dead end: FamilySearch holds only the Napoleonic civil registration for Ovaro's frazioni — Mione, Luincis, Luìnt, Muina, Ovasta, Liariis, Entrampo, Lenzone, Agrons e Cella, Cludinico, Muscletto, Chialina — filmed from the Archivio di Stato di Udine. There are no Ovaro parish books on film anywhere online. The pre-1806 church registers must be asked for at the parish.

name: Imotski
lead: Taken from the Ottomans in July 1717 with a De Franceschi first over the wall. The family has been here three hundred years.
body: Of the seventy Venetians living at Imotski after 1717, only the de Franceschi settled permanently in the Imotska krajina. They held the Perinuša estate — the former begluk of arci-beg Čaušević, with land, houses, a mill and a tower on the Vrljika — and they are still present, physically and in the town's memory, though most of the arable land and the mills are gone and many members have scattered.

There is a long local antagonism to go with it: a persistent belief that the liberation was owed solely to the Imotski Franciscans and the people, which casts the acquisition of Perinuša as a seizure. The estate had in fact been Ottoman crown land, held by begs; who owned it before that is lost in medieval darkness.
Fewer than five people named Franceschi live at Imotski today.

held: FamilySearch film, from HDA Zagreb and Zadar
registers.note: The Podjezerja book runs 1693–1733 and so spans the siege of 1717 itself; Imotski-Glavina picks up in 1731. Both were filmed from the Croatian State Archives.

name: Omiš
lead: A former pirate town at the Cetina mouth, and the Dalmatian family's first seat — a De Franceschi owned a warship here by 1590.
body: The de Franceschi are said to have reached Dalmatia in the fourteenth century as an influential Italian noble house, and to have established themselves at Omiš, where Gaspar de Franceschi is recorded in 1590 as owner of the warship Vascello and later admiral of the fleet.

Zuane Ivan Franceschi sat on the town council here, and it was as an Omiš councillor that he pressed the Imotski refugees' case with the Venetian Provveditore Generale. His estate at Dobrč — today Pisak, along the coast — is where he sheltered them from January 1715.

registers.note: Župa Omiš, 1588–1894. The series opens two years before Gaspar de Franceschi is recorded here as owner of the warship Vascello, which makes this the one place where the Dalmatian family's earliest claim can actually be tested.

name: Split
lead: Twenty-five Franceschi — the largest single concentration of any spelling of this name anywhere in Croatia.
body: Acta Croatica records about sixty people named Franceschi in Croatia today, in thirty households, against fifty in the middle of the last century — an increase of twenty per cent. They are Croats, from Split, and most were born at Split or Imotski.

This is the mirror image of the Istrian story. The Defranceschi of the Pazin area have fallen from about fifty mid-century to about ten; the Franceski of Rijeka from thirty to a single household. Only the Dalmatian branch is growing.

name: Rovinj
lead: The name from 1619 — and the man «da Dignano» buried at Christmas 1728, three weeks after his wife.
body: Rovinj carries the name from **1619**, when a **Pietro De Franceschi** is buried — the entry this archive holds from another direction as «morì ser Piero di Franceschi da Pola», 27 May 1619, and an early dated Istrian record: the Svetvinčenat baptism of 1628 was found after it, and the godparent cells of the name at Svetvinčenat (from 1605) are older.

It does **not** carry it from 1569. The 1569, 1583 and 1592 entries that a surname search returns are **Fracischetto**, **Francoscheto** and **Franceschero** — three other families, and a caution against reading a fuzzy match as a date.

The household that can be followed is **Mattio De Franceschi and Elisabetta**, who baptise **Martino in 1722** and **Benedetto on 23 October 1726**. **Isabetta is buried on 4 December 1728 and Matto on the 27th of the same month** — three weeks apart. And the archive already held that second entry from outside: «**Ob.to di Matt.o de Franceschi da Dignano**». A man described by the Rovinj priest as *from Dignano* had been in the town long enough to baptise two sons there, and buried his wife three weeks before he was buried himself. That the Isabetta of 4 December is the wife rather than a daughter is an inference from the 1722 and 1726 entries, not a statement of the register.
Twenty-one records of ours out of twenty-five indexed, 1619 to 1864, across **twenty-nine volumes opening in 1553** — the largest unread register in Istria that carries the name.

**Re-read on 13 November 2026.** The 1619 entry was looked at again in the burial lists (film 9R2X-VZ9, image 224, left page, first entry: «Adi 27 Maggio … Morse M(esser) Pietro di Fra-ceschi da Pola», level 13, doc). The year is not written in the cell; it is the page's running year, so the date rests on the reader's anchors. Images 223–226 hold **one** such entry, not two, so the «Pietro De Franceschi» and the «Piero di Franceschi» of 1619 may be one man indexed twice (inf). The volume is a camerlengo's list of burials with the fee, not a death register: it gives no parents and no spouse. Its items run from about 1553 to 1672 and 1722 to 1745, not to 1636 as the catalogue says. Only images 190, 203 and 216–228 of the 645 were looked at, so nothing is claimed for the rest.

name: Pula
lead: The see and the port at the foot of Istria — and the town a De Franceschi is called «da Pola» from, in 1619.
body: Carlo's own *L'Istria* lists Franceschi among the noble families of Pola «venuti da Capodistria» before the plague of 1631 — which makes Pula one of the two candidate parents for the southern Istrian clusters, the other being Koper itself.
The earliest dated record this archive holds in Istria names a man of this town rather than of the one he was buried in: **«ser Piero di Franceschi da Pola»**, buried at Rovinj on 27 May 1619.

Pula is also where the church paperwork of the whole south ran. The marriage dispensations entered in the Vodnjan register are issued by the **Ordinariate of Pola** — «dell'Ordinariato di Pola» — and that is the office to write to for what those registers only allude to.

**Pula in the 1890s: two Defranceschi households, one from Ližnjan and one born here.** *The Ližnjan one is told on [the Ližnjan page](/liznjan/#pomer): Antonius, porter of Via Medolino, and his son Antonius Georgius (b. 1894).* **The other is Pola's own — Joannes Baptista Defranceschi, born at Pola on 15 December 1869, a chimney sweep, son of a municipal watchman, Franciscus (dead by 1894), and Euphemia Franca; he married Dominica Francisca Clagnan, a servant of Pola, on 20 January 1894** (`doc`: [the marriage entry](/person/joannes-baptista-defranceschi-1869/), Pula marriages VI, page 139, entry 12). **Their son Alexander Angelus, born 4 January 1893 and baptised in April of that year, was legitimised by the marriage — the baptism entry carries the note** (`doc`: Pula births X, page 19, entry 281; [Alexander's page](/person/alexander-angelus-1893/)). *Three more children are in the index only (Francisca Angela 1891, Angela Regina 1894, Umbertus 1896); the household was in the archive from the index before the pages were read.* *[Households](/households/).*

**Pola's navy parish keeps its own books — and one of them holds a Defranceschi.** *The k.u.k. Kriegsmarine had a parish of its own at Pola; its «Sterb-Register» 1866–1913 and «Trauungs-Buch» 1866–1918 are in German and were read end to end.* **The deaths hold no one of the name. The marriages hold one: on 23 February 1914, in the naval church, Andreas Petešić — a medical petty officer born at Sale near Zara — married [Estella Ida Defranceschi](/person/estella-ida-defranceschi-1893/), born at Gologorica on 11 April 1893, daughter of the farmer Anton Defranceschi and Rosa née Salamon** (`doc`, page 30). *The Gologorica line sends a daughter to Pola's navy; the groom's name is Petešić on the page and «Sečešić» in the later Gologorica census, which this archive has noted rather than settled.*

**Two more Pula burials of the name, read on the pages.** *On 17 September 1877 Francisca, five years old, daughter of a Franciscus, was buried from house 85 (tuberculous meningitis)* — a daughter of Franciscus Defranceschi, **who died two years before her, in 1875, and who is «from Gallignana»** (told next). *On 29 February 1892 a seven-day-old Josephus was buried, «Franciscae domesticae illeg. fil.», the illegitimate son of a servant named Francisca who bore the name — a Defranceschi woman not otherwise placed.* *The Pula civil deaths book has now been read entry by entry, January 1864 to May 1893 (the film has no pages before 1864): **six Defranceschi burials in twenty-nine years, none before 1875** — Franciscus (1875), Francisca (1877), Euphemia and the newborn Joannes (1890), Josephus (1892) and a newborn Antonius (1893); the last four are told above and on the [1890s Pula page](/places/).*

***⭐⭐ And the Pola family comes from Gračišće.*** **On 20 November 1875 «Franciscus fil. Joannis Baptae e Gallignana, uxoratus, diurnista» was buried at Pula, 36, married seven years, of pulmonary emphysema** (`doc`, [the entry](/person/franciscus-liberatus-defranceschi-1840/)). *Gallignana is Gračišće; the father is a Joannes Baptista; the age fits the **Franciscus Liberatus baptised in January 1840 at Gračišće house 5**, a son of Joan. Bapt. Defranceschi, agricola, and Francisca Salomon (`inf`).* **He is the father of the Pola chimney sweep Joannes Baptista (b. 1869) and of the Francisca buried in 1877** — so the first link between the Gračišće line and Pula in this archive is the day-labourer who died there at 36, and the household above is his son's.

***⭐⭐ And his marriage names the parents.*** **On 1 June 1868, in the Pula cathedral (entry 70 of the 1815–1877 marriage book), «Francesco De Franceschi da Gallignana, distretto di Pisino» — 28, a discharged soldier serving as a municipal police guard — married «Eufemia Franca», 25, of Parenzo, a servant who had lived at Pola for thirteen years.** *The entry gives his parents as «Gio. Battista De Franceschi, defunto, possidente» and «Francesca Salomon, defunta»* ([the page](/person/franciscus-liberatus-defranceschi-1840/); `doc`) — the very couple of Gračišće house 5. **So the parentage is no longer an inference; only the choice of which boy — the Franciscus baptised in January 1840, 28 in June 1868 — remains `inf`, and it is a strong one.** Her parents were a Giovanni Franca and a Maria Stifanić. *The Pula civil deaths book, read in order from 1864 to May 1893, holds six Defranceschi burials and none before this man's own in 1875 — the family arrives in the town between the 1860s and 1868.*

***⭐ And the son's baptism, 1869 — the index entry opened.*** **On 26 December 1869, at the cathedral, «Giovanni Battista», born on the 15th, was baptised — the son of «Francesco De franceschi fu Giovanni da Galignano, Daziere» and «Eufemia Franca fu Giovanni da Parenzo»; the godfather is a mason from Tolmezzo, «Matteo Pantelli»** (Pula births 1869–75, Liber VII, p. 92, [image 461](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899F-7DNR?cc=2040054&wc=9R2X-SP8); [his page](/person/joannes-baptista-defranceschi-1869/); `doc`). *This is the baptism the births index pointed to and the archive had not yet opened. It confirms the household and the birth date and adds one thing: the father's work in 1869 was **«daziere»**, a customs guard — between the police guard of the wedding in 1868 and the day-labourer of the burial in 1875.*

***⭐ And the daughter's baptism, 1873 — the burial's «about 1872» replaced by a date.*** **On 23 February 1873, at the cathedral, «Francesca Luigia», born on 1 February at two in the afternoon, was baptised by Don Andrea Juranić — the daughter of «Francesco Defranceschi fu Gio. Batta da Gallignana, distretto di Pisino, Daziere» and «Eufemia Franca fu Giovanni da Parenzo»; sponsors «Matteo Potočnik, fornajo» and «Angela Venezia»; midwife Giovanna Chinol** (Pula births 1869–75, Liber VII, p. 378, entry 91, house 87 Duomo, image 606 of waypoint 9R2X-SP8, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899F-78X3?cc=2040054&wc=9R2X-SP8); `doc`, read at level 13). *It is the same household as the son's baptism above (the husband, the Gračišće father, the Parenzo mother, the work, a customs guard in both) and it is the girl the archive already held as [Francisca, buried on 17 September 1877](/person/francisca-defranceschi-1872/), «five years old», with a birth «about 1872» guessed from that age: she was in fact four years and seven months.* **It adds no person; it replaces a guess with a date, a first name — Francesca Luigia — and a page; and it turns the «`inf`» that her father is the Franciscus buried in 1875 into `doc`.**

***A Defranceschi mother, named at a Pula wedding.*** **In February 1883 the carpenter Antonius Dobrez — born at Visinada on 30 March 1855 and living at Pola since boyhood — married Helena Antonia Cuntu in the cathedral; his mother is entered «Defranceschi Maria».** *The name is on the page, in the parents' cell, beside «Dobrez Joseph, carpentarius»* ([the entry](/person/antonius-dobrez-1855/); `doc`). *It places a household the index had kept unplaced for a month ([h073](/households/)): a Visinada–Kaštelir family whose carpenter son came to Pola — a second road, besides the Gračišće one, by which the name reached the town.*

**And a year later his sister, and a third Pola family from Friuli.** *Catharina Dobrez, born at Visinada on 5 September 1853 and at Pola «from infancy», married the brass-worker Joseph Vio at the cathedral on 25 February 1884 — and again the entry writes her mother «Defranceschi Maria»* ([the entry](/person/catharina-dobrez-1853/), `doc`). **Seven weeks later, on 14 April 1884, a mason called Joannes Baptista «Di Franceschi» — born at Osoppo in Friuli on 1 July 1842 and at Pola since 1864 — married the widow Lucia Dobrila; his parents are «Di Franceschi Joannes» and «Di Cecco Pascha»** ([the entry](/person/joannes-baptista-di-franceschi-1842/), `doc`). *Friulian *di* for Tuscan *de* — the same «of the Franceschi» — but the form is not one of the twelve declared in the scope list, so it is collected, not counted, until David rules. Nothing joins him to the Gračišće family or to the Dobrez household.*

***⭐⭐ A mason and his wife, both Defranceschi, at the font, July 1891.*** **On 26 July 1891 the cathedral baptised «Aloysius Antonius» — born on 5 June at house 10, Via Campo Marzio, to the driver Osualdus Dinon, from Cavasso nuovo, and Catarina Picoli — with the godparents «Defranceschi Antonius, faber murarius» and «Aloysia ejus uxor»; the child bears their two names** (Pula births 1887–96, p. 569, entry 548, [image 315](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-GSKM?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1)). `doc`. *The first page in the archive with a Defranceschi husband and wife together at Pola. Neither has an age, parents or birthplace written. They are `inf` the Aloysia of March 1887, the Antonius of April 1887 and the mason of September 1898 above and below, a trades-circle of one couple; the page does not say so, and the four rows are not merged. The mason is not the Gračišće stonecutter (a lapicida, dead by 1898).*

***A godmother of the name at the cathedral, March 1887.*** **On 6 March 1887 «Defranceschi Aloysia» stood godmother, with the mason «Detoma Antonius», to «Maria Catharina Ursula», born on 9 February 1887 to the mason Jacobus Dilena and Catharina Brenz** (Pula births 1874–87, p. 1117, [image 669](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99F-QJSM?cc=2040054&wc=9R26-BZQ)). `doc`. *The surname is split across two lines in the patrini column and was read at higher magnification. The entry gives no age, parents or house for her, so it says only that a woman of the name was at a Pola font in the spring of 1887; the other Aloysias in this archive are not tied to her.*

***A godfather of the name at the cathedral, April 1887.*** **On 24 April 1887 «Defranceschi Antonius» stood godfather, with «Bilus Catarina», to «Elvira Catarina», born on 16 December 1886 to Carolus Scagnetti and Aloysia Tomsich** (Pula births 1874–87, p. 1133, [image 676](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99F-QJS8?cc=2040054&wc=9R26-BZQ)). `doc`. *The entry gives no trade, age or house for him, so it says only that the name was at a Pola font that spring; the stonecutter of Gračišće, the Ližnjan labourer and the 1898 mason are all possible and nothing in the page chooses between them.*

***⭐ The chimney sweep's eldest, born before the wedding, 1891.*** **On 15 November 1891 «Francisca Angela», born on 27 September, was baptised at the cathedral — the daughter of «Defranceschi Joannes, qm Francisci, e Pola, camini scopator» and «Clagnan Dominica, qm Angeli, e Pola»; the father declared himself before the priest, and a margin note records her legitimation by the marriage of 20 January 1894** (Pula births 1887–96, p. 645, entry 807, [image 340](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99X-GSVF?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1); sponsors «Sissan Petrus, maritimus» and «Nitzer Maria»; midwife Maria Dobrez). `doc`. *She is the first child of the household told above (h047), until now known only from the FamilySearch index; a second, later note dated 23 February 1914 is not read with certainty.*

***⭐⭐ A daughter of the direct line, at Pola.*** **On 14 January 1888, in the cathedral, «Defranceschi Leopolda, ancilla» — born at Gallignana on 6 November 1865, at Pola since 1883 — married the carpenter Emericus Zuban (Zuppan), of Pirano. Her parents are written «Defranceschi Antonius, lapicida» and «Tornasar Maria».** *They are, `inf`, the stonecutter Antonius of Gračišće house 19 (b. 1825) and Maria née Fernasar/Tornasar (1832–1916) — the couple of [the direct line](/direct-line/), so Leopolda is a sister of David's own ancestor* ([the entry](/person/leopolda-de-franceschi-1865/), `doc`). **It is also the first image of Maria's surname: read «Tornasar», with a T that the scribe's own F does not match** ([the comparison](/maternal/fernasar/)). *A servant from the same village, five years in Pola by the wedding, and her father's brother's family already in the town (h129): the Gračišće Defranceschi who came to Pola came more than once.*

***⭐⭐ Her first child, in July 1888.*** **On 15 July 1888, at the cathedral, «Petrus Matthaeus» — born on 29 June at house 231 (Abbazia) — was baptised, the son of «Zuban Emericus, Matthaei e Pyrrhano, faber ferrarius» and «Defranceschi Leopolda, Antonii e Gallignana»** (Pula births 1887–96, p. 143, entry 473, [image 86](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-GQ95?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1); sponsors «Bursich Matthaeus, caterarius» and «Bacich Joannes»; midwife Morin Gabriela). `doc`. *The mother is the daughter of the direct line who had married there on 14 January 1888 (above); the entry gives her father only as Antonius, as the marriage does. A margin note in a later hand — «uxorem duxit Polae 23.II.1914 Annam Pecinić» — says that Petrus Matthaeus himself married at Pola in February 1914. The baptism writes the father's trade «faber ferrarius» (smith) and the marriage entry wrote «carpenter»; the two are as read and not reconciled.*

***⭐⭐ And her second, in April 1890.*** **On 20 April 1890, at the cathedral, «Joanna Maria» — born on 11 January at house 246 (Abbazia) — was baptised, the daughter of «Zuppan Henricus Matthaei, faber lignarius, e Pyrrhano» and «Defranceschi Leopolda, Antonii, e Gallignana»** (Pula births 1887–96, p. 384, entry 261, [image 221](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-G37H?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1); sponsors «Angelovich Joannes, ex-subofficialis marinae» and «Calavar Maria»; midwife Zimprich Maria). `doc`. *The scribe first wrote the father «Emericus» and struck it out for «Henricus»; the 1888 marriage and baptism entries have Emericus, so the correction is not explained. A margin note, partly under a stamp, says the girl married at Pola on 3 August 1914. The trade here is «carpenter», as at the marriage.*

***⭐⭐ And her third, in January 1894.*** **On 6 January 1894, at the cathedral, «Francisca Catarina» — born on 26 November 1893 at house 17 (Via Castropola) — was baptised, the daughter of «Zuppan Henricus, Matthaei, e Pyrrhano, faber lignarius» and «Defranceschi Leopolda, Antonii, e Gallignana»** (Pula births 1893–96, p. 114, entry 9, [image 501](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-GQ1Q?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1); sponsors «Almerigogna Jacobus, carpentarius» and «Blasovich Francisca»; midwife Limpich Maria). `doc`. *Above the father's name stands «vedi Cop. I. n° 449», and a margin note says the girl married «Cvečan Andrea» on 21 October 1915, the parish written «Monfalcone»(?). The scribe again writes the father «Henricus», as for the second child and not «Emericus» as in 1888 (`inf`: the same man). The FamilySearch index had carried her as an unread lead (6YBR-3QNG).*

***⭐⭐ The wife of the 1894 Antonius is found, 1895.*** **On 8 December 1895, at the cathedral, «Joanna Barbara Angela» — born on 24 September at house 6 (Mercato Vecchio) — was baptised, the daughter of «Longhin Vincentius, Thomae, e Venetiis, faber lignarius» and «Rumsich Helena, qm Matthaei, e Besanova»** (Pula births 1893–96, p. 396, entry 821, [image 650](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-GQND?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1); sponsor Ghira Angelus, carpenter; midwife Dobrez Helena). **A margin note reads «nupsit Antonio Defranceschi, Polae 26.X.19?9».** `doc` for the note. *It is the other half of the note on the baptism of [Antonius Georgius, 1894](/liznjan/#pomer) («…Longhini, Polae 26.X.19?9»): the same day and place, each naming the other, so she is his wife (`inf`, firm). The year digits are «19?9» on both, the third a loop that reads as 2 or 0 — most likely 1929, when he was 35 and she 34. No marriage entry has been read.*

***A godmother, December 1895.*** **On 29 December 1895 «Catarina», born that day to the unmarried «Gobbo Catarina, qm Joannis, e Sarmenigga(?)», was baptised at home by the midwife and then received at the cathedral by the canon Pacovich; her sponsors were «Zotel Joseph» and «Defranceschi Catarina»** (Pula births 1893–96, p. 404, entry 865, [image 654](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-GQD1?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1); midwife Zapletal Dominica). `doc`. *The entry gives the godmother no age, trade or kin. The archive's one Catharina of the right place and time is the Gračišće servant born in 1869, [married at Pola in 1898](/person/catharina-defranceschi-kostessich-1869/) — `inf` at most, and the rows are not merged.*

***The foundling's third child, 1896.*** **On 16 May 1896 «Stephanus Petrus», born on 6 May at house 69 (Ponte Castagner), was baptised at the cathedral by the dean; the mother column reads «Franceschi Francisca ex orphanotrophio Tergestino», the father's column is empty; sponsors Rosa Gaspar, smith, and Rosa Josepha** (Pula births 1893–96, p. 465, entry 263, [image 686](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-GQXG?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1); midwife Simecka Dominica). `doc`. *The mother is written in the same words as at [Paula's baptism in 1884](/person/paula-poliak-1884/) and [Joannes Antonius's in 1894](/person/joannes-antonius-franceschi-1894/): `inf` one woman, three children. Giorgio di Montona, muratore», with a wife «Maria Miletich q. Tommaso di Pola», whose four children were baptised at Pola in 1857–63 (Pula births item 2, p. 304, and item 3, pp. 18, 76, 153)** — house 244, in the same town. **That Maria cannot be the widow of 1872: a later note on her marriage entry says she died on 9 August 1863** (told in the next paragraph). **But the same font has a «Maria Franceschini» as godmother three times more: on 23 November 1871 (p. 265, entry 356, a carpenter's son of Duino), on 19 January 1873 (p. 369, entry 33, «Maria France-/schini», read at level 13) and on 21 June 1873 (p. 405, entry 256, now in Latin as «Franceschini Maria», read at level 13, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99F-7ZYC?cc=2040054&wc=9R2X-SP8))** — four times in nineteen months, a Maria of this name standing sponsor at Pola, the second written as the widow of Domenico Franceschi. If the Domenico meant is this one, who died on 1 January 1868, the widow is **Maria Crismanich**, a widow of nearly five years (`inf`, plausible and not proved: the entry gives only a dead husband's name, and another Domenico Franceschi may have lived at Pola). *A near-name, not Defranceschi, and not counted: told because it answers the question the paragraph before it left open.* His brother Luigi-Antonio, a smith of Montona, was married at Pola on 6 February 1861 (Liber IV, p. 29, entry 4, image 375, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-R9QR-Z?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-T3F); `doc`, level 13), the parents given there again as «Giorgio Franceschini» and «Antonia Benvenuti, dead».
