***⭐⭐ And the one who grew up, in 1881 and 1911.*** **On 2 April 1881, at Pola, «Johann Carl», son of «Defranceschi Johann, k.k. Marinediener 2. Cl., aus Galignana in Istrien» and «Paula Petra, daughter of Peter Rocco, Besitzer, from Pola», was born; he was baptised on 19 April. A note added to his baptism entry records that on 10 July 1911 he was married in the Pola cathedral to Ida Revelant** ([the baptism](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99X-PWSZ?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-K6L); [his page](/person/johann-carl-defranceschi-1881/); `doc`). **His bride's own baptism is now read:** *[Ida Rosa Francisca Revelant](/person/ida-rosa-francisca-revelant-defranceschi-1876/), born at Pola on 27 April 1876 to a mason from Tarcento in Friuli and Theresia Fortis of Modena, legitimised by their marriage in Italy in 1878, carries the note «juncta est matrimonio die 10. VII. 1911 cum De Franceschi Joanne»* ([image](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99F-79LK?cc=2040054&wc=9R26-BZQ), `doc`). *He is one of two of the couple's five known children to reach adulthood (the other is Raimund Johann, above). The cathedral marriage book of 1911 has not yet been read for him; it should name his bride's parents and his own.*

***⭐⭐ A little girl, in 1882.*** **On 4 August 1882, at Pola, «Francisca Antonia Defranceschi, ehel. Tochter des Johann Defranceschi, k.k. Marine-Dieners», born at Pola, aged 4½, died of diphtheria and was buried on the naval cemetery the next day** ([the entry](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99X-RV4S?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-FMQ); [her page](/person/francisca-antonia-defranceschi-1878/); `doc`). **`doc` that she is Johann and Paula's daughter: her baptism at Pola names «Defranceschi Johann, k.k. Marinediener 2. Cl., aus Galignana in Istrien» and «Paula Petra, daughter of Peter Rocco», and gives her birth as 24 January 1878** ([the baptism](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-PWXX?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-K6L); baptised 17 September 1878). * Seven months later her mother died of lung tuberculosis (next entry); eight years after that their son.*

***⭐⭐ And his wife, twelve years on.*** **On 27 February 1883, in the civil hospital at Pola, «Defranceschi Paula Pietra, Gattin des Johann Defranceschi, k.k. Marine-Diener 2. Cl.» died of lung tuberculosis, aged 31½, born at Pola, daughter of «Peter Rocco, Landtaglöhner»; she was buried on the naval cemetery on 1 March** ([the entry](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-RN6X?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-6YS); [her page](/person/paula-pietra-defranceschi-1851/); `doc`). *She is Paula Pietra of the 1871 marriage — the husband's name and rank, the birthplace Pola and the age agree, and the father's «Rocco» recurs; no child is named, and his own death and any second marriage are still not found.*

***⭐⭐ And their boy, seven years after that.*** **On 10 November 1890, in the civil hospital at Pola, «Defranceschi Eugen Josef, ehel. Sohn des Johann Defranceschi, k.u.k. Marine-Diener», born at Pola, aged 14, died of a fractured skull; he was buried on the naval cemetery on 12 November** ([the entry](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99X-RKX2?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-N35); [his page](/person/eugen-josef-defranceschi-1876/); `doc`). **`doc` that he is the child of Johann and Paula Pietra: the naval baptism book has «Eugen Josef», born at Pola 8 December 1875, baptised 26 February 1876, son of «Defranceschi Johann, k.k. Marinediener 3. Cl.» and «Paula Petra»** ([the baptism](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-2H4B?cc=2040054&wc=9R2C-K68)). *He was 14 years 11 months old at death. Johann's own death is not found.*

**And the Dobrez brother, a third time.** *On 19 February 1898 Franciscus Paulus Maria Dobrez — a shoemaker born at **Parenzo** on 28 August 1865 — married Joanna Zonta of Veglia; his mother is again «Defranceschi Maria»* ([the entry](/person/franciscus-paulus-maria-dobrez-1865/), `doc`). *Three weddings at Pula (1883, 1884, 1898) now name Maria Defranceschi as the mother of Dobrez children born at Visinada, Kaštelir and Parenzo: she is a woman of the Poreč hinterland, and her own baptism is the entry still to find there.*

***⭐ And the youngest sister, baptised at Pola in 1867 — with her mother's father named.*** **On 15 December 1867 «Egidia Maria», born on 17 September, was baptised at the cathedral — the daughter of «Giuseppe Dobrez fu Antonio da Verpinaz, marinajo» and «Maria Defranceschi fu Antonio da Visinada»** (Pula births 1857–68, Liber VI, p. 362, entry 344, [image 372](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99F-76SQ?cc=2040054&wc=9R2X-SP8); [her page](/person/egidia-maria-dobrez-1867/); `doc`). *This is the fifth Dobrez child of the household, and the first read on a baptism page rather than a wedding: the family is **at Pola in 1867**, two years after the youngest brother was born at Parenzo, the father then a sailor (a carpenter on the 1883–84 weddings). And it names **Maria's father — «fu Antonio», of Visinada, dead by 1867**: the first thing the archive has about her own family. The midwife's cell reads «Maria Defranceschi» as well — the same name; whether the mother is written twice, the clerk slipped, or a kinswoman delivered the child, the page does not say. A margin fraction «23/18 over 8/71» may mark the girl's death in August 1871 (`inf`; the 1871 death book is not read).* *The Visinada Antonio is still to be placed: no Defranceschi Antonio of the Vižinada–Kaštelir cluster in the archive has a daughter Maria on a read page.*

***A midwife named Dobrez, in the 1868–71 baptism book — and a second Dobrez family from Veprinaz.*** **Through the Pula births book of 1869–75 (Liber VII, read page by page to p. 377, 23 February 1873) the midwife's cell reads «Maria Dobrez» (written «Dobreg» and «Dobrec» too) on dozens of entries (at least 73 by p. 111, and many more since), and on several she herself baptises «per urgenza».** *Whose wife she is the pages do not say.* Beside Joseph Dobrez of h073, whose wife is Maria Defranceschi, the book holds a second Dobrez household: **«Matteo Dobrez fu Andrea da Veprinaz, distretto di Fiume (Volosca)», calafato in 1868 and falegname in 1871, with «Agostina» (Cergnan, then Fregnar, di Francesco, of Fersato near Fiume)** — a son Francesco Matteo, baptised 16 August 1868 (entry 275), and a daughter «Maria Egidia», born 13 November 1871 and baptised on 3 December (p. 267, entry 156, image 550, the midwife «Maria Dobrez» on that page too). **A third child of Matteo's household is on p. 372: «Nicolò Antonio», born 27 January 1873 and baptised on 2 February, son of «Matteo Dobretz fu Andrea da Leprinaz presso Volosca, falegname» (the village's name read at level 12 as «Leprina…», the Veprinaz of the other entries) and «Giustina Cernjar di Francesco da Fiume» (entry 56, image 603, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99F-7Z7L?cc=2040054&wc=9R2X-SP8); `doc`; the midwife this time Antonia Gotthardi, not Maria Dobrez).** The wife's name has been written Agostina Cergnan and Fregnar before; the Fiume father Francesco is the same. Joseph's father is «Antonio» of Veprinaz, Matteo's «Andrea» of the same village: two Veprinaz Dobrez families at Pola in the same years, and a Dobrez midwife who may belong to either. `inf`, undecided: one reading is that she is Matteo's wife, not Maria Defranceschi, since Matteo's household has children baptised through these same years; but nothing on the pages ties her to either man, and the page of 1867 that wrote «Maria Defranceschi» in the midwife's cell for Joseph's own daughter shows the clerks were not always careful. *No entry of the name Defranceschi was found beside any of them in the 1869–71 pages read.*

***⭐ And a child from Medulin, in the war.*** **On 8 November 1915, at Pola, «Ivan Defranceski», born at Medulin and aged 3½, died of pneumonia and heart failure; he was buried on 10 November** ([the entry](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899F-XDHQ?cc=2040054&wc=9R2F-927); [his page](/person/ivan-defranceski-1912/); `doc`). *The entry names no parents. He is born about 1912, in the parish where the surname otherwise appears only through daughters; the Medulin baptism of that year is not on the film.*

***⭐⭐ And another Ivan, five weeks later — from Ližnjan.*** **On 10 December 1915, at Pola, «Ivan Defrančeski — Antoni e Justina Visdarich», born at Ližnjan, aged 7, died of scarlet fever and was buried on 11 December** ([the entry](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899F-X8GP?cc=2040054&wc=9R2F-927); [his page](/person/ivan-defranceski-1908/); `doc`). *A different child from the Medulin boy above. His parents are named; the archive has no Justina Visdarich and no Antonio of the right age with a read register, so the family is not yet placed.*

***⭐ A widower's second marriage at Pola, 1824 — the index's Francesco opened on the page.*** **On 18 November 1824, at Pola, «Francesco De Franceschi», agricoltore, aged 48 and a widower («vedovo»), married «Domenica Filipich», aged 38 and unmarried; his parents are written «Michael De Franceschi, morto» and «Maddalena Bubich, morta», hers «Giorgio Filipich, morto» and «Maria Filipich, sua moglie, morta»; the witnesses are «Martin Cetich» and «Francesco Ugo», both unmarried, and the priest Don Giovanni Cuizza, cappellano curato** (Pula marriages 1815–77, Liber III, p. 10 for the groom and his parents and p. 11 for the bride's parents, witnesses and priest, image 269 of waypoint 9R28-T3F, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-R9SN-9?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-T3F); `doc`, read at level 13; no house number is given for either of them). *This is not a discovery: the FamilySearch index already held the couple* — two rows «Francesco De Franceschi, b. 1776, spouse Domenica Filipich, parents Maddalena Bubich and Michael De Franceschi» (6YB5-XFRY and 6YB5-XFRB) — *and the roster holds a Pula burial «Francesco De Franceschi, b. 1775, d. 1827»* (1:1:6BKV-2V6P). **What the page adds is the age, 48, which makes the index's «1776» an age-derived year, and the widowhood.** The man of the burial of 1827 is very probably this one — the same name, the same town, and an age that fits (`inf`; the burial entry itself is not yet read, and the two roster rows are not merged). *What is not known:* his first wife and any children (the first marriage lies before 1815, in the 1685–1818 prose book of the same film, not yet walked); where his parents Michael and Maddalena came from — **Bubich is a surname of Gologorica in this archive's own registers, and nothing on this page links him to that village** (`inf`, no more than a coincidence of a name). **Next: the burial of 1827 at Pola (9R2Z-4WB, Pula deaths 1716–1864) and his first marriage.**

***The Vodnjan weaver Cristoforo De Franceschi as a witness at Pola, 1835.*** **On 30 April 1835 «Giovanni Roditti q. Anastasio and Bernardina da Vanzo», a widower of Dignano, and «Andrianna Biasiol di Francesco and Antonia Francin» (the bride's mother a Francin, the near-name, not counted), of Dignano, were entered in the Pola marriage book — the marriage itself was made at the parish office of Dignano, where the papers lie, and the Pola entry only records it; the witnesses are «Cristoforo De Fran-/ceschi q. Giuseppe, Tessitore» and «Luigi Fabro, Sarto»** (Pula marriages 1815–77, Liber III, p. 41, image 284 of waypoint 9R28-T3F, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-R9S2-6?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-T3F); `doc`, the surname split across the line end and read at level 13: «De Fran-» then «ceschi»; the priest was Don Giacomo Dari, curato). *Dignano is Vodnjan, and a «Cristoforo De Franceschi di Giuseppe — Tessitore», a weaver, a brother of the priest Don Stefano, is already in this archive as a witness at Vodnjan in 1818* ([his row](/person/cristoforo-de-franceschi-1824-2/)). **The father's name, the trade and the town agree, so this is almost certainly the same man, seventeen years on (`inf`, firm): a Vodnjan weaver of the name lending his signature, here his name only, to a neighbours' wedding.** *It adds no person; it adds a date to a weaver's life (alive on 30 April 1835) and a second witness-line to the one the archive had.* **The Vodnjan marriage book of 1835 holds the original entry** (not yet read for this couple).

***⭐ A mother «di Franceschi» in a Trieste bride's marriage entry at Pola, 1863 — new in this book.*** **On 4 February 1863, in the cathedral, «Andrea-Nicolò Petris di Pola, Negoziante», aged 32, house 303, was married to «Catterina-Cristina Ilovar di Trieste», aged 25, house 320** (Pola marriages 1858–73, Liber IV copulatorum, p. 61, entry 6, image 392 of waypoint 9R28-T3F, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99X-R9Q8-5?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-T3F); banns read on 16, 21 and 23 November 1862; `doc`). **The parents' page (p. 62) names the bride's parents as «Giuseppe Ilovar, cattolico, Mastro-muratore» and «Maria di / Franceschi: cattolica: defonta»** — her mother, already dead — the line broken after «di», the surname plain and ending in -chi, read at level 13 on the page image (`doc` for the entry as written). The first letter of the family name is an I-shaped capital in the bride's cell and the same in the father's, so «Ilovar» is the reading and «Novar» is not excluded (`inf`). **The entry gives the mother no age, no birthplace and no father; it does not say where the couple lived, and the only town it names is the bride's, Trieste.** «Di Franceschi» is a spelling the archive's own scope list counts, so it is told here; whether she belongs to the Defranceschi stock the page does not say, and **she is not merged with any row**. Before saying so, the archive's `sources.json`, `searched.json` and `roster.json` were searched for the names Ilovar, Novar and Petris: none stands in them, so this is a first sight and not a re-read. **Next:** the bride's baptism at Trieste about 1837 (aged 25 in February 1863), and her parents' marriage, probably at Trieste in the 1830s, are the two records that could name this Maria's own father and place; neither has been opened.

***The last of the old Pula baptism books, 1800–1817, and the confirmation lists bound behind it — read 13 November 2026 (FamilySearch 9R2X-SPV, film 392388301, 79 images, the continuation of the births book 1767–1817).*** **One book, in two series, no table:** Italian paragraphs under a centred «Adi …», 22 September 1800 to 2 February 1812 (ending «Finis»), then a second series from 2 February 1812 to 16 December 1817; the catalogue's «Baptisms 1773–1825» is wrong for this film, which holds no baptism after 1817. Behind the baptisms are lists of confirmations: Pola cathedral 1773–92, 1792–96, 1797–1801 and 3–6 October 1825, and a list of men dated January 1815. **The baptisms (images 7–54, every page displayed by readers at page size, none of it zoomed except where said): no Defranceschi baptism, no Kovačina, no Kalanj.** **One cell is a candidate and is not settled:** on 1 October 1813 (image 45 right, old folio 165) «Francesco Sacco(?)», born 29 September, son of «Domenico De Fran… q.m Zuanne» and «D.a Margherita nata Baldin…», godparents Antonio Gabrie… and Francesca Artusi (`doc`; at level 13 I can read «De Franc-» with a flourish for the ending, and I do not read Franceschi: the letters after c are not settled, and this is the form Defranca of the Atlas at most). **The confirmation lists, where the name stands plainly (`doc`, level 13, checked by me on the saved zooms):** in the list of June 1792 (image 67 right, p. 187) a sponsor «Elena de Francarki», a sponsor «Lucia di Franceschi» and a candidate «… filia Jacobi di Francaschi» (the scribe's *a* and *e* are alike, so the spelling is Francaschi/Franceschi); in the list of 6 October 1825 (image 60 left, folio 180, under the head «idem», i.e. Promontore) «**Nadalina De Franceschi di Gregorio**» and «**Maria De Franceschi q.m Matteo**». Further cells of the 1792 group, read by the readers at page size only and not yet zoomed: a child of Bartholomeus de Franceschi, a sponsor Michael, a Lucia with a sponsor Mathea, a Maria. ***⭐ And the men's list of January 1815 names Pomer.*** **«Francesco De Franc[e]sch[i] q.m Michiel — Pomer — 43 — ammogliato»** (image 77 right, folio 198, signed by the parish priest Giovanni Cuzza; read at level 13, the ending of the surname a flourish — `doc`, the surname's last letters not settled). `inf:` this is the Francesco whom the Pula marriage of 18 November 1824 calls the widower, 48, son of «Michael De Franceschi, morto» and «Maddalena Bubich, morta»: the same father's name, an age (43 in 1815, 48 in 1824) that agrees to within a year, and married in 1815, so a widower by 1824. It puts the family of Michael at **Pomer** in January 1815, a generation before Tomas «son of the late Michele», farmer at Pomer house 5, married in 1843 ([the Pomer page](/places/pomer/)). The two Michaels are not proved to be one man. Not read or not settled: the margin notes squeezed beside the baptisms on images 21, 23, 24, 26, 27 and 30; faded entries of 1813 (images 43–44); a «Michiel Ca?lay» of 24 April 1814 (image 47 left), which has the ending of a Kallayn-type name and was not zoomed. Near-names seen and not counted: Fraggiacomo, Frazza/Franza, Francin, Demori, Deghenghi, Calagher/Callagher, Calabro, Calluciola, De Cal-, Cailens, Marinoni «detto Kalizzan» (a by-name).

***The Pula baptism book 1767–1800, read to its end on 13 November 2026 — and one mother of the name, in 1772 (FamilySearch 9R2X-BZ9, film roll 37, 136 images; register images 5–131, 15 August 1767 to 22 December 1800).*** **On 13 December 1772** the cathedral baptised «Antonio Lorenzo», born on the 8th, «figlio di m.r Antonio Vio q. Cro…, e di D.a Maria nata **De Franceschi** di lui legittima consorte», by the curate Don Niccolò Leonardelli, godparents Pietro Cipriotto q. Francesco and Antonio Artusio q. Giandomenico (image 23 right, page 37, folio 19; level 13, checked by me on the saved zoom: «De» and «Franceschi» are plainly separate words; `doc`). It is the family name at Pula as a bride's, thirty years before the Francesco of the Pomer list: Maria's father, her place of origin and her husband's trade are not given, and nothing joins her to any other person of the archive. **Nothing else in the book, at the readers' page-size reading:** no child of a De Franceschi father, no Michael with a Maddalena, no Francesco born about 1772–76 baptised at Pula, no Matteo, Gregorio, Jacobus or Bartholomeus De Franceschi, no Kovačina, no Kalanj-type surname. That statement rests on sonnet readers who displayed every opening (22 folders of six images), not on a walk by eye; the form «Deffranceschi» was not typed to them, and the leads of the Atlas were not; the cells below were not zoomed. Gaps and open cells: the left page of image 125 (page 220, «31 Genaro 1799») is under a pasted flap and almost all unread, an entry of 8 March 1799 is covered by a slip (image 124 right), the same opening was photographed three times (images 42–44, slips of June 1778) and images 65–70 and 95–100 are faded; Cal-/Ca- cells (Calegher, Calich of Pomer, Caligari, Calurri, «Cal?ick» of 4 June 1799, «Catabar/Calabar» of 24 January 1792) were not zoomed and none looked like a Kalanj form. Near-names not counted: Franco, Francovich, Getni, De Mori, Deghenghi, Fragiacomo, Frezza, De Vescovi, a «Francesco de Fran.co» patronymic of Bergamo (1769, zoomed), and a godmother «Agata ved.a di Francesco Fancesi/Pancesi» of 1792 (no r after Fa-, zoomed). The film overlaps the next one by one opening (22 September 1800, folio 232); there are no confirmation lists here, they are bound in 9R2X-SPV.

name: Kaštelir
lead: Seventeen records, and — read together with Vižinada and Tar — one family across three parishes.
body: Kaštelir was for a year the densest thing in Istria this archive could document and could not explain: seventeen records of the name, four of them accepted, a hilltop village kept under Vižinada, and no lane on the branch chart running through it.

Read by image rather than by place text, the three parishes of the Poreč hinterland turn out to hold **the same people**. **Giulio (Julius) De Franceschi × Maria Ceselin** — the name is written Ceselin, Sesalin and Cedelini in three different hands — has a son **Francesco Napoleone baptised at Vižinada on 7 September 1818**, a daughter **Catharina baptised at Kaštelir in 1829**, and is himself buried at **Kaštelir on 19 September 1854**, entered as «Giulio Defranceschi, of Mattio». **Francesco Napoleone** then raises his own family at Kaštelir with **Maria Radojković** — Aloisia 1859, Josephus 1862, Margarita 1869.

A second household runs alongside it: **Angelus Defranceschi × Lucia-Antonia Rodella**, whose son **Julius is baptised at Kaštelir on 29 January 1866** and **buried at Tar on 9 March 1870**, aged four. Angelus dies at Tar in 1895.

**A third Kaštelir family leaves by the back door: Joseph Dobrez × Maria Defranceschi.** *Their daughter Catharina is baptised at Kaštelir on 8 September 1853* (index); *their son Antonius, a carpenter, was born at Visinada on 30 March 1855 and was at Pola «from boyhood» when he married there in February 1883 — and that marriage entry writes his mother «Defranceschi Maria»* ([the Pula wedding](/person/antonius-dobrez-1855/), `doc`; [h073](/households/)). *Maria is a Defranceschi by birth, and her own baptism is the thing still to find in the Vižinada–Kaštelir books.*

The join is by name, date and parish adjacency — no single document names two of these places at once — so it is an inference, and is marked as one. But it is the first time the hinterland has read as a family rather than as a scatter.

And it corrects this page's neighbour: **Draguč, long counted at twenty-five records, holds none.** Its three volumes were fetched and every image tested. The twenty-five were Vižinada's, returned twice by a search parameter that does not filter.

name: Bakar
lead: The deep-water bay east of Rijeka, and one of the Kvarner parishes where the surname sits in the registers with no line yet attached to it.
body: Bakar belongs with Rijeka and Ledenice in the group of Kvarner parishes this archive can name people in but cannot yet join to any line. The households here are treated as **unplaced** — documented, and honestly unattached — rather than folded into the Carnia or Pazin-county descent on the strength of a shared surname.

name: Draguč
lead: Twenty-five records that were never here.
body: This archive's parish table has carried **Draguč, 25 records, 1784–1851** since September. On 13 September 2026 the parish's three volumes were fetched from FamilySearch and every image in them tested against a pool of 1,768 indexed records of the name. **None matched.**

The twenty-five were **Vižinada's**. FamilySearch's place parameter is a relevance boost and not a filter, and the two parishes return the same records in the same order — a thing this archive tested and published on 9 September, then went on using the number anyway for four more days.

Draguč is left on the map because the correction is worth more than the deletion. Its books exist and open in 1784; nothing says the name cannot be in an unindexed page of them. What is settled is that **nothing in the index puts it here**.

name: Premantura
lead: The last village before the cape at the bottom of Istria, and one of the southern parishes the surname holds in.
body: Premantura sits with Ližnjan, Fažana, Šišan and Vodnjan in the southern Istrian group. The households here are documented in the sweeps but not yet worked through a register page by page, which is the only method that has produced generations in this part of Istria.

name: Fažana
lead: Forty-two records, every one of them ours — and most of what this archive has been calling the Pula cluster.
body: Fažana has been a single dot on the branch chart reading «baptisms and deaths at Fasana through the 1810s, 1840s and after». Read by image it holds **forty-two records of the name between 1770 and 1855, and not one of them belongs to another family** — a cleaner return than any Istrian parish except Ližnjan.

Two households. **Vittorio De Franceschi × Stella Tamborin** — written Etella, Steffa and Samburin by four different hands — baptise Perina on 23 April 1810, Vittorio in 1813, and **Natale Mattio on 21 April 1816**. **Giuseppe De Franceschi × Giovanna Beluzzi** baptise Elisabetta in 1810 and **Irene on 13 October 1816**; a Giovanna «of Giuseppe Defranceschi» is buried as early as 1770.

Those names matter. This archive's sweep table names the **Pula** cluster's people as «Natale Mattio, Angelo, Vitorio, Elisabetta, Irene De Franceschi». **Natale Mattio, Vittorio, Elisabetta and Irene are Fažana's**, four miles up the coast — another town-name supplied by a search that could not see a town.
One entry keeps two surnames at once: **«Petrina Tamburin or Defranceschi», 1807.**

name: Telve
lead: In the Valsugana, east of Trento — the largest single concentration of the name outside Istria and Dalmatia in this archive's roster.
body: Twenty-two people of the surname in this archive sit at Telve, more than at any Istrian village except Vodnjan. They come out of David's family tree rather than out of a register this archive has read, and **no descent connects them to the Istrian or Carnian families**. Defranceschi is a common Trentino surname formed independently from the same patronymic; that is the working assumption here and it is an assumption, not a finding.
Telve is listed so the twenty-two are visible and counted, not folded into a line they may have nothing to do with.

name: Laives
lead: South of Bolzano in the Adige valley — a second Tyrolean cluster, and like Telve unattached to any Istrian line.
body: Eleven people of the name, from the family tree rather than from a register read here. Laives belongs with Telve, Strigno and Fiera di Primiero in the Trentino–South Tyrol group: same surname, different formation, **no documented connection to Istria**.

name: Strigno
lead: A Valsugana village a few kilometres from Telve, with the same surname and the same open question.
body: Grouped with Telve and Fiera di Primiero. Counted here rather than absorbed into an Istrian line.

name: Torrington
lead: A brass town in the Naugatuck valley of Connecticut, and the largest American landing-place in this archive.
body: Twelve people of the name in Torrington. The New England brass and clock towns took Istrian and Trentino labour in the same decades that Brooklyn took the Gallignana families, and this is where a cluster of them settled.
Nothing here has yet been checked against a federal census or a naturalisation file. **That is the next step for this place**, and it is the method that worked for the Eleven in Brooklyn.

name: Pfullingen
lead: Below the Swabian Alb, near Reutlingen — where the German leg of David's own line came to rest after 1947.
body: Anton Rudolf Defranceski appears on the Pfullingen list of foreigners in 1947 and was certified by that town's mayor in 1950. Pfullingen, Reutlingen, Neuhausen an der Erms, Metzingen and Bad Urach are one small district, and the family's German years happen inside it.
This is the leg of the journey that a walking itinerary is still owed for.

name: Postira
lead: On the north shore of Brač, with three reconstructed households of the name.
body: Postira sits with Omiš and Split in the Dalmatian group. Three households here were reconstructed from indexed records; none has been read register-page by register-page.

name: Santa Maria di Sala
lead: In the Veneto between Padua and Venice — a mainland Venetian parish carrying the name.
body: Six people, from the tree rather than from a register read here. Relevant because the Venetian line of this archive — the printers, the Grand Chancellor, the Omiš and Zadar families — is a Venetian-state story, and mainland parishes of the Republic are where its ordinary people would be.

name: Šterna
lead: «Bortolo figlio del q. Gio: Batta de Franceschi dalla Cargna» — the sentence this archive has been looking for since it began.
body: **«Alli 12 9bre 1777. Cepich. Cargna.**  Bortolo figlio del q. Gio: Batta de Franceschi **dalla Cargna**, Diocese d'Udine, ha contratto legitimo Matrimonio coll'Ill.ma Sig.a **Zanetta Gravisi** figlia dell'Ill.mo Sig.r **Marchese Nazario** della Villa di Cepich di questa Pieve, e ciò previo il di lui libero stato ottenuto dall'Ill.mo Monsig.r **Gio: Domenico Stratico Vesc.o di Cittanova**… nec non essendo stati dispensati dalle trine pubblicazioni solite farsi…»**  Read off the film at full magnification on 13 September 2026.

**This is the entry that had never been found.** The Svetvinčenat reading page says it plainly: *«What the film has not given is an origin. Not one entry in fourteen years of baptisms says where these people came from. No «da Carnia», no «di Mione», no «q. di Agrons». The Carnian identification of this household still rests entirely on the company it keeps.»* Here the priest writes it himself, in the body of the entry and again in the margin: **Cepich. Cargna.**

And the bride is a **Gravisi** — not a coincidence of spelling but the Capodistrian marquisal house, named in full: *the Illustrious Signor Marchese Nazario*, of the village of Cepich in this parish. A man from Carnia whose father is already dead marries a marquis's daughter, with the Bishop of Cittanova certifying his free status because nobody in Istria could, and with the three readings of the banns waived.

**A correction to this page, published within hours of the claim it corrects.** This archive wrote on the morning of 13 September that *«Gio Batta De Franceschi and Zanetta Gravisi… stand behind two entries in the marriage book as the parents of the groom»*. They are not the parents. **Zanetta Gravisi is Bortolo's wife.** The index lists groom, groom's father, bride, bride's father, and this archive read the four names as two couples. The page says otherwise and the page wins.

So the household reads: **Gio: Batta de Franceschi**, of Carnia, dead before 1777 and never in an Istrian register. His son **Bortolo × Zanetta Gravisi**, married 12 November 1777 — and their children baptised at Šterna from the following September: **Felice Anto 27 September 1778**, **Mariana February 1786**, **Federico 14 March 1794**, **Catarina 11 August 1797**, with a Francesco «of Bortolo» buried on 20 December 1787. The mother written *Zannetta*, *Zanetta*, *Giovana* and *Giovanna* by four hands is the same marchese's daughter. Then a second **Gio: Batta and Maria** baptising in 1807 and 1809 — the grandfather's name come round — and in July 1819 the burial of a **Bartolo, son of that Gio: Batta and Maria**. *(Corrected: this page first read that 1819 burial as Bortolo the elder «at the end of it». The entry names parents, so it is a child — a grandson carrying the grandfather's name. Bortolo's own death has not been found.)*

**The reading is confirmed twice.** Filmed with the register is an archivist's pencil finding-aid slip listing the book's notable entries, and it independently records: *«12/XI 1777 Bortolo figlio del q. Gio: Batta de Franceschi dalla Cargna con Ill.ma Sig.a Zanetta Gravisi figlia dell'Ill.mo Sig. Marchese Nazario — pag 39»*. FamilySearch's index counted that slip as a second record, which is why this archive expected two marriages and found one.

**And the parish is older than this page first said.** Šterna's filmed books were given here as running 1723–1836. They do not: the first volume is a composite of **births from 1667**, with marriages from 1688 and deaths from 1667, running to 1727. **It holds no De Franceschi at all** — 207 images, tested one by one against every record of the name this archive can reach. Which fits: there is no family of the name here in the seventeenth century, and then a man arrives from Carnia and marries a marquis's daughter in 1777.

**Who the Gravisi were.** Josip Banić's *Venetian Istria in the embrace of a nascent Dominium* (CEU doctoral dissertation, 2021) sets it out from the archival record. **Niccolò de Gravisi, son of the late Vanto, of Piran** — distinguished citizens, not nobles — uncovered a conspiracy against Venice at Padua. By a ducale of Doge **Francesco Foscari dated 10 March 1440**, he was invested with the fort of **Petrapilosa** in Istria as a hereditary fief of the Republic: «overtaken by the zeal of true loyalty… he revealed the conspiracy plotted against us and our state in Padua», so that «the very city of Padua remains preserved under our Republic». The fief was worth 150 ducats a year, the balance of his pension paid by the treasury of Koper; he was to guard the castle at his own expense and give Venice, **every St Mark's day, one candle weighing ten pounds** for the Church of St Mark. He was **not** given the *merum et mixtum imperium* — blood justice and civil appeals stayed with the podestà of Koper.

Because Petrapilosa had been the **seat of the Istrian margraves**, the house took the title *marchiones* — **the Marquises of Petrapilosa**, whom Banić calls «the most prestigious noble house of late medieval Istria», nobles «unlike any other on the entire Istrian peninsula». *(He also corrects the standard account: Venturini's 1906 family history credits Niccolò with uncovering the 1435 Marsilio conspiracy; the documents say the 1439 Scrovegni one.)*

**Petrapilosa's country is this country.** Its jurisdiction sits in the Buzet uplands with **Hum and Roč** — the same small world as Šterna, Sovinjak and Draguč. So «the Ill.mo Sig.r Marchese Nazario» whose daughter Bortolo married in 1777 is of that house, in its own territory. **What that does and does not mean.** Three hundred and thirty-seven years separate Doge Foscari's grant from this wedding, and by 1777 the Gravisi were many branches deep; a marchese living at a village like Cepich is a cadet line, not the seigneur of the castle. What the entry shows is a man who arrived from Carnia with a dead father and no Istrian parish to vouch for him marrying into the titled family of the district. Inferred — that this Nazario is of the Petrapilosa house, from the title and the district

**And one structural thing worth keeping.** Banić's population tables name only two **feudal jurisdictions** in Venetian Istria: **Petrapilosa and Svetvinčenat.** Those are the two places this archive finds the surname thickest — Svetvinčenat with 118 records from 1628, and the Šterna household in Petrapilosa's country. Seigneurial lords recruited settlers in a way communes did not, which is exactly the mechanism a Carnian immigration would use. Inferred — the coincidence is suggestive, not demonstrated

**And the district has a name and a shape.** Banić's population tables put **Buzet** at 151 hearths with «300 in the contado, *including Petrapilosa*» — and the district's later count of 4,844 is given as «**including Hum and Roč, Sovinjak, Vrh and Draguč, and the villages around Rašpor**». So Šterna, **Sovinjak** and **Draguč** — three places this archive has been treating separately — sit inside one documented administrative block, the Buzet contado with Petrapilosa's feud in it. When Venice took the Margraviate over, «the old tributes were confirmed and no new taxes introduced» in **Roč and the villages of Petrapilosa** — the citation for which is Klen's edition of the **1425 Petrapilosa tax roll**, at pages 96–97.

**The fief was the castle and twelve villages.** In **1483** Niccolò's four sons — **Vanta, Michele, Pietro and Gravis** — divided the holding: the castle itself stayed in common, «and the brothers took turns administering it, a year each». Which twelve villages they were is the one thing this archive now wants and does not have. They are in **Danilo Klen, «Urbar Petre Pilose iz 1425. godine», *Starine* 58 (1980): 85–124** — a household-level tax roll of this country, edited and printed. **It is not online.** Starine 58 is catalogued at the Croatian Academy's digital library as *In Copyright*, with no scan; four physical copies sit in the HAZU Library in Zagreb (A1-003-058, A-003-058, ČA-003-058, PA-003-058). It is a reading-room or scan request, not a download.

name: Vrsar
lead: One household, five entries, sixteen years: a christening, a widowing and a death, and then the name stops.
body: **Francesco De Franceschi and Giacoma** baptise a son, **Luca, on 11 August 1670**. **Giacoma is buried in 1683.** A **Marga «of Francesco»** is buried on 19 August 1686. **Francesco himself is buried on 26 November 1686.**

That is the whole of the name at Vrsar — five entries, three of them burials, inside sixteen years. The parish has four volumes from 1613 and nothing of the family before 1670 or after 1686. A household arrived, was recorded, and ended or moved on.
Orsera is on the coast between Poreč and Rovinj, twelve kilometres from Svetvinčenat, where a De Franceschi household is documented from 1628.

name: Plomin
lead: Above its bay on the eastern Istrian coast, at the Kvarner end of the county of Pazin.
body: Three people of the name. Plomin sits on the road between the Pazin county villages and the Kvarner shore — the same route the Carnia line is inferred to have taken to Fiume.

name: Paluzza
lead: In the Val But of Carnia, on the road to the Plöcken pass — one of the valleys the 1679 headmen's list covers.
body: Paluzza belongs with Mione, Ovaro, Muina and Givigliana in the Carnian group. The documented link to Istria is the 1679 list on which a Zuane De Franceschi of Mione is recorded working in the County of Pazin with his son; Paluzza is on the map because the walking itinerary crosses it, not because a person of the name is yet documented here.

name: Sovinjak
lead: Two burials, twenty-four years apart, and both of them a son of a Gio Battista.
body: The register holds exactly two entries for this parish and they are the whole of what is known. **Zuane Franceschi, buried at Sovignacco in 1759, son of Gio Batta Franceschi.** **Sebastiano De Franceschi, born and buried on 6 August 1783, son of Gio Battista De Franceschi** — an infant, dead in the same year he was born.

One small hill parish above Buzet; two sons of a man of that name a quarter of a century apart. It is either a father who buried a child in middle age and another in old age, or it is two generations putting the grandfather's name back into use — which is what this family does in every place where it can be watched long enough to see.

Neither reading can be tested yet. **Sovinjak is not one of the forty-three Istrian parishes in the filmed collection this archive has walked**, and no register of it has been found on any film reachable from here. The town sits on the Buzet upland with Roč, Hum, Draguč and Šterna — four more parishes carrying the name and three of them equally unfilmed. Until one of those books opens, the household stays a pair of burials and a shared Christian name.

The place was reached not by searching for it but by asking a duller question: which towns in this archive's own register have no entry in this archive's own atlas? Twenty-one did. Sovinjak was one of only five whose rows turned out to carry the family's name at all.

**And it is not as isolated as this page assumed.** Banić's figures for the Buzet contado name its constituent places outright: **Hum and Roč, Sovinjak, Vrh and Draguč, and the villages around Rašpor** — with Petrapilosa's feud inside the same count. Sovinjak is not a stray hill parish; it is one village of a district that also contains **Šterna**, where a Bortolo de Franceschi *dalla Cargna* married the daughter of a Marchese Gravisi in 1777, and **Draguč**, which holds none of the name at all. Whether the two sons of a Gio Batta buried here in 1759 and 1783 belong to that Šterna household is not shown by anything — but they are now in the same administrative country rather than in unrelated places. Inferred — shared district, not a shared family

name: Tar
lead: A man of sixty-seven buried here in 1895, and the four-year-old son he had buried twenty-five years before.
body: **Angelus Defranceschi, born 1828, died 23 April 1895 and buried at Tar the following day.** His wife is written only as **Julie**. In the same book, twenty-five years earlier: **Julius, born 1866, dead on 8 March 1870 and buried on the 9th**, son of *Angeli Defranceschi* and *Luciæ Rodella*.

So the wife the burial entry calls Julie is named in the child's entry as **Lucia Rodella**, and the boy was given his mother's name in its masculine form. That is the whole household: one couple, one child who did not live, and a man who outlived the boy by a quarter of a century.

Tar is four volumes in the filmed collection, opening in 1815 — so this household *can* be read, and has not been. It sits in the country behind Poreč with Kaštelir, Vižinada, Šterna and Draguč, the block this archive calls the Poreč hinterland: about sixty entries between them, no lane running through any of them, and not one page read by eye.

name: Pomer
lead: A Defranceschi household at house 5 from 1843 — Tomas, Magdalena Buich and three children — a daughter's nine Lazaro grandchildren, and a widow who was the village midwife.
body: Pomer sits on the bay south-east of Pula. It entered this archive on 13 September 2026 as one of twenty-one towns found in its register and missing from its atlas, on the strength of three rows spelt **Defrančichi**, none of them ours. It turned out to hold more of the name than most villages that are supposed to.

**The books were read end to end on 13–14 October 2026** — births 1816–1900 (86 frames), marriages 1837–1865 and 1885–1910, deaths 1842–1911 — and the result is a household, not a name: **Tomas Defranceschi, a farmer, son of the late Michele, married Maddalena Buich on 16 August 1843** and they had **Lucia (1844), Michele (1847, died at fourteen) and Maria (1852)** at house 5. Tomas died of typhus on 5 April 1858. A baby born to the widow in 1859 — father not named — is the Stephanus Buić who carries on in the books as «filius Magdalenae De-franceschi», with eight children of his own.

**Maria went to Medulin**, where she married Petrus Kirac and had eight children; **Lucia stayed**, married **Matheus Lazaro** in January 1866, and had **nine children 1866–1884, six of them dead before they were nine**. Their youngest, Catharina (b. 1884, d. Pula 1954), married Joannes Zuccon in 1905 — the entry that first found Lucia, because a wedding has to name the bride's mother.
**Magdalena Buich**, Tomas's widow, was born at Pomer in July 1816 and is written as the village **midwife** in 1868, 1880 and 1882 — in a book that otherwise names only Rakić, Vojak and Fabac women.

A **second household of the name** appears in 1886: Antonius, son of Antonius, **from Ližnjan**, a labourer at house 17, father of Mathias. It is not joined to Tomas's — and the Pula marriage book of 1890 shows he was born at Ližnjan in 1848, moved to Pula, lost his wife Euphemia there on 1 May 1890 and married again.
**Not found:** where Tomas and Michele came from before Pomer, and the deaths of Magdalena, Lucia and Stephanus. Full account and every entry on [the Ližnjan page](/liznjan/#pomer).

**Pomer in January 1815 — one step further back.** *The list of men bound into the Pula baptism book 1800–1817 (FamilySearch 9R2X-SPV, image 77 right, folio 198, level 13) has «Francesco De Franc[e]sch[i] q.m Michiel», from «Pomer», 43, married.* `inf:` the man whom [the Pula page](/places/pula/) holds as the widower of 1824, 48, son of Michael De Franceschi and Maddalena Bubich: a Pomer family of Michael is thus on paper in 1815, a generation before the Tomas «son of the late Michele» of 1843 above. It is not proved that Michael here and Michele there are one man, and the surname's last letters on the 1815 list are a flourish.

name: Krbune
lead: One volume, 124 images, and a De Franceschi daughter's whole family inside it.
body: Krbune is a hamlet in the County of Pazin, four kilometres from Gologorica — the same small country this archive's own line lives in. FamilySearch has **one book** of it, 124 images.

That book holds **Mariana De Franceschi and Vincentius Marziol**: **Maria**, **Rosaria** 1833, **Franciscus** 21 November 1836, **Anna** 16 November 1839, **Antonia** 17 March 1843 — and four further entries where the couple stand godparent to other families' children.

She looked like several women because the index spells her husband four ways — *Marziol*, *Marizo*, *Marjas*, *Marjiol* — and her own name *Mariana*, *Marianna*, and in the Croatian orthography of the 1830s **«Marianna Defrančeški»**. One woman, one village, eleven entries.
She is **not** the Mariana De Franceschi born at Šterna in February 1786; that one would have been fifty-seven at the last of these births.

name: Dubrovnik
lead: Fifty-six records with no town written on them, and a family of the name in the old Republic.
body: Dubrovnik is the largest thing in this archive's index that has never had a page. Resolved through the films their images sit on, **fifty-six records** of the name belong to the city parish and to **Pile** outside the western gate — against the twenty-two and sixteen the parish table has carried. Not one of them says «Dubrovnik» in its place field.

The household that can be followed is a **Marietta Defranceschi**, daughter of a **Pietro Defranceschi**, who marries **Matteo Persich** — later written **Peršić** — and whose children are baptised in the city: **Cattarina Teresa Vittoria Maria in 1863** and **Giustino Antonio Alberto Lucciano in 1871**. An Antonio Persich marries a Maria Defranceschi in 1853. The 1829 entry that names Pietro is a marriage, forty-two years before the last of the children, so more than one generation of Persich is in these rows and this page will not pretend to sort them yet.

Nothing joins any of it to the Venetian line at Zadar, Omiš and Imotski, or to Istria. Ragusa was a separate republic with its own patriciate and its own trade, and a Franceschi there needs its own argument, not an inherited one.

name: Labin
lead: The oldest books in the Istrian catalogue — from 1536 — and a family that only shows up three centuries into them.
body: Labin's eleven volumes open in **1536**, the earliest of any Istrian parish FamilySearch has filmed, and they have never been read here.

The archive has carried «Labin 1615 — Aloÿsius Defranceschi» as **the single earliest indexed occurrence of the surname anywhere in Istria**. Read by image against the parish's own books, that entry is not in the pool this archive can see, and the records that *are* run **1826–1866**. The 1615 is not withdrawn — it may sit in a harvest this pass did not reach — but it is not confirmed either, and the honest statement is that Labin's confirmed run begins two centuries later than the page has implied.
Six of the fourteen indexed hits are **Franceschich, Francescich, Francocich** — Slavic formations of the same root, and not this family.

What is here is a married-out daughter and her family: **Dominica Defranceschi × Antonius Zustovich**, with children baptised **1853, 1857, 1861, 1864 and 1866**. Earlier, in 1824 and 1827, a **Maria Defranceschi** stands in two marriage entries as the mother of the parties.

name: Medulin
lead: Four records at the southern tip, and a Maria Defranceschi whose children married Voinich.
body: Medulin is the third of the southern-tip parishes, with Ližnjan and Premantura, and its books open in **1648**.

Four records of the name, and they are marriages rather than baptisms: **Josephus Grahalich in 1828** and **Martinus Rakich in 1831**, both weddings in which a **Maria Defranceschi** and an **Antonius Voinich** stand as the bride's parents; and **Lucas Kivac in 1874**, whose mother is a Maria Defranceschi married to Petrus Kivac.

Which means the De Franceschi presence here is visible **only through daughters** — the surname never appears on a child of the name, only on the mothers of other families' children. It is the clearest small example of what the lost-daughters queue was built to catch. **One qualification, from Pola: a boy «Ivan Defranceski», born at Medulin about 1912, died at Pola on 8 November 1915, aged 3½** ([the entry](/person/ivan-defranceski-1912/)) — so the name was borne by a child in Medulin in the 1910s; the books on the film stop in 1890, so he cannot yet be placed.

name: Galižana
lead: One entry, and it carries the surname this archive spent a day chasing at Vodnjan.
body: Galižana holds a single record of the name, a marriage of **1824**, and it is worth a page for what is in it: the groom is **Giacomo Giachin**, and a **Domenica Defranceschi** is named among the parties.

**Giachin** is the surname behind an open question at Vodnjan. A *Michiela De Franceschi fu Giuseppe* is named in the Vodnjan death register of February 1833 as the mother of a **Giacomo Giachin**; and the Vodnjan marriages carry a **Sebastiano Giachin × Domenica De Franceschi**, 1817–1832. Here is a Giacomo Giachin marrying at Gallesano in 1824 with a Domenica Defranceschi in the entry.

The index writes one of the parties as **«Sebastiano Defranceschi»**, which is almost certainly wrong — a Giachin father given the mother's surname by a transcriber, a failure this archive has seen before. **The page will say and the index will not**, and until the page is read this is a coincidence of names in a neighbouring parish and nothing more.

name: Kršan
lead: Two De Franceschi women marry two Domazetović men in twelve years — and one of them is a Gologorica woman.
body: Kršan holds five records of the name and they are all of one kind. **Anna Maria Francisca De Franceschi × Thomas Joachimus Clemens de Domazetovich** — children baptised **1881, 1883 and 1887**. **Clotildis Adelaidis Defranceschi × Rudolfus Stanislaus de Domazetovich** — children in **1893 and 1894**. Two women of the name, two men of one family, inside twelve years, in a parish where the surname appears nowhere else.

And the first of them is not a stranger. This site's Gologorica page has carried her since September: **«Anna Maria Francisca, born at Gologorica 28 October 1860, married a Domazetovich, died at Trieste on 22 June 1941.»** The roster had her birth as 1880 — which would have made her a year old at her first child's baptism — and the two records were never set beside each other until the pedigree gate refused to draw her chart and the refusal had to be explained.

So the Kršan marriages reach back to **Gologorica**, the village of this archive's own line, thirty kilometres north-west. Whether Clotildis Adelaidis is her sister the register does not say, and this page will not guess.

The index spells the husband's name four ways across three entries — *Thomas Joachimus Clemnet*, *Thomas Joachimus Celmes De Domazetovich*, *Thomas-Joachimus-Clemens Domazetovich* — which is the ordinary condition of this material and the reason a name alone settles nothing.
